stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes the fundamental difference between a shear force diagram and a shear force influence line for a statically determinate beam?

choices.A: A shear diagram shows the internal shear at a specific point for all possible load positions, while an influence line shows the internal shear at all points for a fixed load position.
choices.B: A shear diagram shows the internal shear at all points along the beam for a fixed load position, while an influence line shows the internal shear at one specific point as a unit load moves across the beam.
choices.C: A shear diagram is used exclusively for dynamic moving loads, while an influence line is used exclusively for static dead loads.
choices.D: For a statically determinate beam, a shear diagram consists of straight lines, whereas an influence line is always composed of parabolic or cubic curves.

id: 0311. Design of Steel Components – Tension Members
stem:
A steel tension member consists of a 6 in wide by 3/8 in thick plate with two bolt holes in a single line across the width. The plate is connected with 7/8 in diameter bolts.
The steel has a yield strength \( F_y = 50 \,\text{ksi} \) and an ultimate tensile strength \( F_u = 65 \,\text{ksi} \).
Ignore any shear lag effects.
Use ASD method to determine the allowable tensile strength (in kips) of the member and identify the governing limit state.
answer: Allowable strength \( \dfrac{P_n}{\Omega} =48.8 \,\text{kips}  \), governed by net section fracture.
sourceSubtopic: Structural Design → Design of Steel Components

id: 0310. Design of Steel Components – Tension Members
stem:

Ignore any shear lag effects.
Use LRFD method to determine the design tensile strength (in kips) of the member and identify the governing limit state.
answer: Design strength \( \phi P_n =73.1 \,\text{kips} \), governed by net section fracture.

stem: A ball starts from rest and slides down a \(30^\circ\) incline. After \(4\ \text{s}\) its speed reaches \(6\ \text{m/s}\). Assuming constant acceleration along the plane, how far will the block travel in the next  \(6\ \text{s}\)?

A test vehicle moves along a circular ramp of radius \(r=40\ \text{m}\). At the instant of interest its speed is \(v=18\ \text{m/s}\), and it is still accelerating tangentially with angular acceleration  \(\alpha=0.5\ \text{rad/s}^2\). Determine the magnitude of the acceleration (in \(\text{m/s}^2\)).

A block initially at rest is acted upon by a constant horizontal force of \(18\ \text{N}\) for \(3\ \text{s}\). After the force is removed, the block continues to move at a constant velocity and covers a distance of \(80\ \text{m}\) during the following \(10\ \text{s}\). Determine the mass of the block in kilograms.

A soccer ball is kicked from level ground with initial speed \(v_0 = 40\ \text{m/s}\) at an angle \(\theta = 45^\circ\) above the horizontal. Neglect air resistance and use \(g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^2\). Find the horizontal range \(R\).

Two particles start from the same location at the same instant and move in a straight line. Particle A has initial speed \(u_A = 6\ \text{m/s}\) and constant acceleration \(a_A = 1.5\ \text{m/s}^2\). Particle B has initial speed \(u_B = 2\ \text{m/s}\) and constant acceleration \(a_B = 2.5\ \text{m/s}^2\). They arrive at the same point at the same time. How long (in seconds) do they travel?
A car is traveling along a straight highway at a speed of \(72\ \text{km/h}\). It comes to rest uniformly in a distance of \(200\ \text{m}\). Find the stopping time \(t\) in seconds.

A small drone is flying north with a speed of \(36\ \text{km/h}\). A steady wind suddenly blows toward the east, perpendicular to the drone’s motion. After the wind begins to act, the drone’s resultant ground speed becomes \(45\ \text{km/h}\). What is the magnitude of the wind’s velocity component?

A small remote-controlled boat needs to cross a 120 m wide lake. In still air, the boat can travel straight across in 3 minutes. However, when a steady crosswind begins to blow, the boat must aim slightly into the wind in order to reach a point directly opposite its starting location. Under these conditions, it takes 4 minutes to cross. What is the wind’s velocity in m/min?
A cyclist rides from home to a lakeside trail at \(12\ \text{mph}\) and returns along the same route at \(18\ \text{mph}\). What is the average speed (mph) for the entire round trip?

A small object moves along a straight path with uniform acceleration \(a_0 = 4\ \text{cm/s}^2\). During the 10th second, it travels \(43\ \text{cm}\). Determine the initial velocity \(v_0\) in \(\text{cm/s}\).
A commuter train moves at 54 km/h and comes to rest uniformly in 12 s. Determine how far from the platform the brakes should be applied.

A cargo drone flies horizontally at \(100\ \text{m/s}\) and drops a small package from an altitude of \(300\ \text{m}\). Neglecting air resistance, what will be the package’s speed (m/s) after \(4\ \text{s}\) of free fall? Use \(g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^2\).

A rescue drone flying horizontally at a constant altitude of \(400\ \text{m}\) releases a supply package with a horizontal speed of \(120\ \text{m/s}\). Neglecting air resistance, how far horizontally (m) will the package travel before it reaches the ground?  Assume \(g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^2\).

A drone releases a small package vertically upward from a height with an initial speed of \(10\ \text{m/s}\). After \(4\ \text{s}\), the package reaches the ground. Assuming \(g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^2\), find the release height \(h\) (m) of the drone.

A race car moves along a curved test track described by \(y = 0.05\,x^{2}\). At the point where \(x = 200\ \text{m}\), its speed is \(v = 25\ \text{m/s}\) and its tangential acceleration is \(a_t = 3\ \text{m/s}^2\). Determine the magnitude of the acceleration at this instant.
references:
FE Reference Handbook 10.5 P102, 103:

 Dynamics- Particle Kinematics – Normal and Tangential Components

of \(30\ \text{m/s}\).

The vehicle starts exactly at the \( x \)-axis (\( \theta = 0 \)) at time \( t = 0\,\mathrm{s} \) and travels with a constant transverse velocity of \( 30\,\mathrm{m/s} \). At time \( t = 10\,\mathrm{s} \), the angle \( \theta \) from the \( x \) axis to the position vector \( \mathbf{r} \) is most nearly:

A ball is projected vertically upward from a height of \( 6 \, \mathrm{ft} \) above the ground with an initial velocity of \( 65 \, \mathrm{ft/sec} \). Neglecting air resistance, the maximum height above the ground that the ball will reach is most nearly:

A car is traveling at \( 48 \, \mathrm{mph} \) when the driver sees the traffic light turn yellow. The yellow phase lasts for \( 4.5 \, \mathrm{s} \), and the intersection ahead is \( 160 \, \mathrm{ft} \) wide. What constant acceleration is required for the car to just clear the intersection at the exact moment the light turns red? The acceleration is most nearly:
A car with a mass of \(1500\ \text{kg}\) is traveling at \(72\ \text{km/h}\). If the car comes to a complete stop in \(20\ \text{m}\), determine the average braking force required (in newtons).

Two forces act on a \(0.25\,\text{kg}\) object:

\(\vec F_{1}=4\mathbf i + 3\mathbf j – 5\mathbf k\ \text{N}\)

and

\(\vec F_{2}=-2\mathbf i + 4\mathbf j – \mathbf k\ \text{N}\).

Determine the magnitude of the acceleration of the object in \(\text{m/s}^2\).

stem: A ball experiences a constant force \(\vec{F} = 6\mathbf i – 4\mathbf j + 3\mathbf k\) N and moves through a displacement \(\vec{s} = 2\mathbf i + \mathbf j – \mathbf k\) m. Determine the work done by the force (in J).

A winch pulls a boat-and-trailer of total mass \(m=900\ \text{kg}\) up a launch ramp that makes an angle  \(\theta=12^\circ\) with the horizontal. The cable reels in so that the boat moves at a steady \(v=0.60\ \text{m/s}\). Neglect rolling resistance and losses. Determine the mechanical power (W) delivered by the winch.
A \(5\ \text{kg}\) object is released from rest and falls freely under gravity. Determine its kinetic energy (in joules) after \(t = 3\ \text{s}\) of fall, neglecting air resistance.

A hoist lifts a load of \(200\ \text{kg}\) vertically upward at a constant speed of \(0.25\ \text{m/s}\). Determine the power output (in J/s) required by the hoist motor. Neglect energy losses and assume steady motion.

A constant horizontal force of \(F = 30\ \text{N}\) pushes a \(1.5\ \text{kg}\) block up a smooth incline that rises \(25^\circ\) above the horizontal. If the block moves a distance of \(5\ \text{m}\) along the incline, find the work done by the horizontal force. Ignore the effect of gravity and friction.
When a spring is compressed by \(10\ \text{cm}\), its potential energy is \(25\ \text{J}\). Determine the force (in newtons) required to compress the same spring by \(25\ \text{cm}\).
A \(12\ \text{kg}\) object is dropped from a height of \(80\ \text{m}\). Neglecting air resistance, determine its kinetic energy (in joules) when it is \(50\ \text{m}\) above the ground.

A \(5\ \text{kg}\) object is released from rest and falls freely under gravity. Assume the initial height is \(h_0 = 50\ \text{m}\) above the ground. Determine its potential energy (J) after \(t = 3\ \text{s}\) of fall (ignore air resistance).

A motor delivers 3.00 kW of power to a pump that lifts water vertically 5.0 m from a well. The overall efficiency of the motor–pump system is 80%. Neglecting losses in the piping, determine the mass of water (in kg) that can be pumped in 1.0 min.

A well is \(10\ \text{m}\) deep and \(2.0\ \text{m}\) in diameter. Only the bottom \(2.0\ \text{m}\) contains water. A pump at the bottom empties the water in \(20\ \text{min}\). Estimate the required power (hp), neglecting losses.

A \(1500\,\text{kg}\) car moves down a \(20^\circ\) incline with initial speed \(v_1=14\,\text{m/s}\).Brakes are applied and the car comes to rest uniformly after traveling \(s=30\,\text{m}\) along the slope.Using the nonconservative work–energy relation, find the average braking force \(F_b\) in kN.

A \(6\ \text{kg}\) ball is dropped from a height of \(4\ \text{m}\) onto a soft surface.

The ball continues to move \(0.15\ \text{m}\) into the surface before stopping.

Assuming the resisting force of the surface is constant, determine the average resisting force (in newtons).
A body is dropped freely from a height of \(H = 40\ \text{m}\). At what height \(y\) above the ground will its kinetic energy be three times its remaining potential energy?

A baseball of mass \(0.145\ \text{kg}\) is pitched horizontally toward a batter with a speed of \(38\ \text{m/s}\). Take the direction from the pitcher to the batter as the positive \(x\)-axis. The batter hits the ball, and it leaves the bat with a speed of \(46\ \text{m/s}\) at \(25^\circ\) above the horizontal, traveling back toward the pitcher. Determine the magnitude of the impulse (in kg·m/s) delivered to the ball by the bat.

A \(0.25\ \text{kg}\) soccer ball is moving horizontally toward the west with a speed of \(18\ \text{m/s}\). A player kicks the ball so that it leaves the foot with a speed of \(24\ \text{m/s}\) at an angle of \(40^\circ\) north of east. Determine the magnitude of the net impulse (in kg·m/s) delivered to the ball by the player’s foot.

A \(0.5\ \text{kg}\) drone is flying horizontally toward the east with a speed of \(12\ \text{m/s}\). A sudden gust of wind acts on the drone and changes its velocity to \(15\ \text{m/s}\) at a direction of \(30^\circ\) north of east. Determine the magnitude of the net impulse (in kg·m/s) delivered by the wind to the drone.

A \(3,000\ \text{kg}\) truck is moving north at \(12\ \text{m/s}\). A \(1,500\ \text{kg}\) van is moving south at \(16\ \text{m/s}\) toward the truck. The collision is perfectly inelastic, and the two vehicles stick together. Find the combined velocity (m/s) of the wreckage and specify its travel direction.
answer: \(2.67\ \text{m/s}\) in the travel direction of the truck (north).

stem: A \(900\ \text{kg}\) compact car is traveling east at \(22\ \text{m/s}\). A \(1,400\ \text{kg}\) SUV is traveling west at \(18\ \text{m/s}\) toward the compact car. The two vehicles collide and lock together. Determine the magnitude and direction of the combined velocity immediately after impact.
answer: \(2.35\ \text{m/s}\) in the travel direction of the SUV (west).

stem: A \(1.2\ \text{kg}\) ball \(A\) moves to the right at \(4.0\ \text{m/s}\) along a smooth, horizontal surface. A horizontal force of \( 10\,\mathrm{kN} \) is applied to the centroid of the block. If the coefficient of static friction between the block and the surface is \( \mu_s = 0.25 \), which of the following statements is most nearly correct regarding the block’s impending motion?

choices.A: The block will not move; the maximum static friction force is \( 6.13\,\mathrm{kN} \).
choices.B: The block will move; the maximum static friction force is \( 6.13\,\mathrm{kN} \).
choices.C: The block will not move; the maximum static friction force is \( 24.5\,\mathrm{kN} \).
choices.D: The block will move; the maximum static friction force is \( 2.50\,\mathrm{kN} \).

stem: The average velocity of fluid in a pipe is calculated using the equation \( v = \frac{Q}{A} \). The volumetric flow rate is measured as \( Q = 0.50 \ \mathrm{m}^3/\mathrm{s} \) with a standard uncertainty of \( \sigma_Q = 0.02 \ \mathrm{m}^3/\mathrm{s} \). The cross-sectional area is measured as \( A = 0.10 \ \mathrm{m}^2 \) with a standard uncertainty of \( \sigma_A = 0.005 \ \mathrm{m}^2 \). Assuming uncorrelated variables, what is the expected standard uncertainty of the calculated velocity, \( \sigma_v \)?

The volume of a solid rectangular block is calculated using \( V = L W H \). The measured dimensions and their independent standard uncertainties are \( L = 10.0 \ \mathrm{cm} \) with \( \sigma_L = 0.1 \ \mathrm{cm} \), \( W = 5.0 \ \mathrm{cm} \) with \( \sigma_W = 0.1 \ \mathrm{cm} \), and \( H = 2.0 \ \mathrm{cm} \) with \( \sigma_H = 0.05 \ \mathrm{cm} \). What is the expected standard uncertainty of the calculated volume, \( \sigma_V \)?

The electrical power dissipated by a resistor is given by the formula \( P = I^2 R \). The measured current is \( I = 5.0 \ \mathrm{A} \) with a standard uncertainty of \( \sigma_I = 0.1 \ \mathrm{A} \). The measured resistance is \( R = 10.0 \ \Omega \) with a standard uncertainty of \( \sigma_R = 0.2 \ \Omega \). Assuming the uncertainties are uncorrelated, what is the expected standard uncertainty in the calculated power, \( \sigma_P \)?

A total length \( L \) is calculated by combining three independent component lengths using the linear equation \( L = f(x_1, x_2, x_3) = x_1 + 2x_2 + x_3 \). The standard deviations (uncertainties) of the measured components are \( \sigma_{x_1} = 0.1 \ \mathrm{cm} \), \( \sigma_{x_2} = 0.2 \ \mathrm{cm} \), and \( \sigma_{x_3} = 0.3 \ \mathrm{cm} \). What is the expected standard uncertainty of the total length, \( \sigma_L \)?

During a series of structural load tests, a load cell consistently reads \( 50 \ \mathrm{lbs} \) higher than the actual applied load due to improper zeroing. The variation between individual readings of the same static load fluctuates by \( \pm 2 \ \mathrm{lbs} \). Which of the following statements correctly identifies the error components in these measurements?

choices.A: The \( 50 \ \mathrm{lb} \) offset is a random error, and the \( \pm 2 \ \mathrm{lb} \) variation is a systematic error.
choices.B: Both the \( 50 \ \mathrm{lb} \) offset and the \( \pm 2 \ \mathrm{lb} \) variation are random errors.
choices.C: The \( 50 \ \mathrm{lb} \) offset is a systematic error, and the \( \pm 2 \ \mathrm{lb} \) variation is a random error.

A trapezoidal open channel has a bottom width of \( b = 4.0\text{ ft} \) and symmetrical side slopes of 2:1 (\( 2\text{ horizontal} : 1\text{ vertical} \)). If the flow depth is \( y = 2.5\text{ ft} \), calculate the hydraulic radius (\( R_H \)) of the channel.

A municipal wastewater collection system is being designed. A \( 30 \)-inch-diameter concrete sewer pipe is installed at a uniform slope of \( 0.008 \, \mathrm{ft/ft} \). Assuming the Manning’s roughness coefficient \( n \) is constant with depth and equal to \( 0.014 \), determine the expected flow velocity of the water when the pipe is flowing exactly half-full.
sourceTags: Open-Channel Flow and/or Pipe Flow of Water

stem: An impulse turbine wheel operates by receiving a continuous water jet (\( \rho = 1000 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^3 \)) directed at its moving blades. The total flow rate delivered by the nozzle is \( Q = 0.15 \ \mathrm{m}^3/\mathrm{s} \), and the absolute velocity of the jet is \( v_1 = 30 \ \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s} \). The turbine wheel rotates such that the blades move in the same direction as the jet at a constant tangential velocity of \( v = 15 \ \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s} \). If the geometric design of the blades deflects the water by an angle of \( \alpha = 120^\circ \), determine the theoretical mechanical power (\( \dot{W} \)) generated by this impulse turbine.

A continuous water jet (\( \rho = 1000 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^3 \)) is directed at a series of moving blades on a turbine wheel. The total flow rate from the nozzle is \( Q = 0.2 \ \mathrm{m}^3/\mathrm{s} \) and the absolute jet velocity is \( v_1 = 30 \ \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s} \). The blades move in the same horizontal direction as the jet at a constant linear velocity of \( v = 15 \ \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s} \). If the curved blades deflect the water forward by an angle of \( \alpha = 60^\circ \) relative to the horizontal, calculate the magnitude of the horizontal force (\( F_x \)) exerted on the moving blades.

A water jet (\( \rho = 1000 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^3 \)) exits a nozzle with a steady volumetric flow rate of \( Q = 0.1 \ \mathrm{m}^3/\mathrm{s} \) and an initial absolute velocity of \( v_1 = 20 \ \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s} \). The horizontal jet strikes a stationary hemispherical blade (deflector) that completely reverses the direction of the flow, deflecting it by \( \alpha = 180^\circ \). Assuming ideal flow with no frictional losses across the blade surface (\( v_2 = v_1 \)), calculate the magnitude of the horizontal force (\( F_{blade} \)) exerted by the fluid on the fixed blade.

A large holding tank filled with water (\( \gamma = 9810\text{ N/m}^3 \)) has a circular orifice on its side. The area of the nozzle tip is \( A_2 = 0.01\text{ m}^2 \). The height of the water surface above the centerline of the outlet is maintained at a constant \( h = 5.0\text{ m} \). Determine the horizontal propulsive force (\( F \)) exerted on the tank by the exiting jet.

A primary water transmission line features a vertical \( 90^\circ \) flanged pipe bend that redirects the flow upward. The constant-diameter pipe has an internal diameter of \( D = 0.5\text{ m} \) and carries water (\( \rho = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3 \)) at a steady volumetric flow rate of \( Q = 0.5\text{ m}^3\text{/s} \). The gauge pressure at the exit of the bend (Section 2) is \( P_2 = 200\text{ kPa} \). The volume of water contained within the short-radius bend is \( V = 0.15\text{ m}^3 \). Assuming frictional losses across the bend are negligible, what is most nearly the magnitude of the y-component force (\( F_y \)) exerted by the fluid on the pipe bend?

Water (\( \rho = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3 \)) flows through a horizontal \( 90^\circ \) pipe bend of constant diameter \( D = 0.5\text{ m} \). The volumetric flow rate is \( Q = 0.5\text{ m}^3\text{/s} \) and the gauge pressure at the inlet (Section 1) is \( P_1 = 200\text{ kPa} \). Assuming frictional losses are negligible (\( P_1 \approx P_2 \)), calculate the magnitude of the x-component force (\( F_x \)) exerted by the fluid on the pipe bend.

A straight horizontal reducing nozzle discharges water (\( \rho = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3 \)) directly into the atmosphere (\( P_2 = 0\text{ kPa gauge} \)). The flow rate is \( Q = 0.1\text{ m}^3\text{/s} \). At the inlet (Section 1), the area is \( A_1 = 0.05\text{ m}^2 \), the velocity is \( v_1 = 2.0\text{ m/s} \), and the gauge pressure is \( P_1 = 150\text{ kPa} \). At the exit (Section 2), the velocity is \( v_2 = 5.0\text{ m/s} \). Calculate the reaction force (\( R_x \)) required to hold the nozzle in place.

A ramjet engine inlet operating at high speeds encounters a normal shock wave just inside the diffuser. The air (\( k = 1.4 \)) enters the shock at a Mach number of \( Ma_1 = 1.8 \) and a static pressure of \( P_1 = 50 \ \mathrm{kPa} \). As the fluid traverses the shock, kinetic energy is violently converted to pressure. Use the normal shock relationships to determine the static pressure ratio (\( P_2 / P_1 \)) across the wave.

During the operation of a supersonic blowdown wind tunnel, a normal shock wave forms in the constant-area test section. The air (\( k = 1.4 \)) immediately upstream of the shock is traveling at a Mach number of \( Ma_1 = 2.5 \) and has a static pressure of \( P_1 = 30 \ \mathrm{kPa} \). The normal shock causes an abrupt deceleration and compression of the fluid. What is most nearly the downstream Mach number (\( Ma_2 \)) immediately after the shock wave?

A converging-diverging (De Laval) nozzle is being designed for a solid-propellant rocket motor. The combustion gases are approximated as ideal air (\( k = 1.4 \)). To achieve the desired thrust, the flow must expand isentropically from sonic conditions at the throat (\( Ma = 1.0 \), area \( A^* \)) to a supersonic Mach number of \( Ma_e = 3.0 \) at the nozzle exit plane. What is most nearly the required area ratio (\( A_e / A^* \)) of the exit area to the throat area?

A pitot-static tube is utilized to measure the airspeed of a high-performance aircraft operating in the transonic regime. The aircraft is flying at a Mach number of \( Ma = 0.85 \) through air (\( k = 1.4 \)). The static pressure port on the instrument reads the ambient pressure \( P = 40 \ \mathrm{kPa} \). Assuming the deceleration of the air at the pitot tube’s stagnation point is an isentropic process, what is most nearly the ratio of the stagnation pressure to the static pressure (\( P_0 / P \))?

A stagnation temperature probe is mounted on the nose of a supersonic military aircraft. The aircraft is traveling at a Mach number of \( Ma = 2.0 \) through ambient air (\( k = 1.4 \)) that has a static absolute temperature of \( T = 220 \ \mathrm{K} \) and a static pressure of \( P = 26 \ \mathrm{kPa} \). Assuming the air is brought to rest isentropically at the tip of the probe, what is most nearly the stagnation temperature (\( T_0 \)) recorded by the sensor?

A commercial jetliner is cruising at an altitude of \( 10,000 \ \mathrm{m} \). The aircraft’s true airspeed is determined to be \( V = 250 \ \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s} \). At this altitude, the ambient static temperature of the air (\( k = 1.4, \ R = 287 \ \mathrm{J}/(\mathrm{kg}\cdot\mathrm{K}) \)) is measured at \( -40^\circ\mathrm{C} \). What is most nearly the Mach number (\( Ma \)) of the aircraft?

A supersonic wind tunnel is being prepared for aerodynamic testing of a new airfoil profile. The working fluid is dry air, which behaves as an ideal gas with a specific heat ratio of \( k = 1.4 \) and a specific gas constant of \( R = 287 \ \mathrm{J}/(\mathrm{kg}\cdot\mathrm{K}) \). Sensors in the test section record a static absolute pressure of \( P = 45 \ \mathrm{kPa} \) and a static temperature of \( T = -20^\circ\mathrm{C} \). What is most nearly the local speed of sound (\( c \)) in the test section?

As part of an industrial cogeneration power plant, hot combustion gases (modeled as ideal air with a constant specific heat of \( c_p = 1000 \ \mathrm{J}/(\mathrm{kg}\cdot\mathrm{K}) \)) enter an axial-flow gas turbine. Sensors record a steady mass flow rate of \( \dot{m} = 2.5 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{s} \) with an absolute inlet temperature of \( T_i = 800 \ \mathrm{K} \). After expanding through the turbine stages, the exhaust gas temperature drops significantly to \( T_e = 400 \ \mathrm{K} \). Assuming the expansion process is ideal and adiabatic with negligible changes in kinetic and potential energy, what is most nearly the theoretical mechanical power (\( \dot{W}_{turb} \)) produced at the turbine shaft?

A typical backward curved fan is used in an HVAC duct system. The fan generates a pressure rise of \( \Delta P = 600 \ \mathrm{Pa} \) (\( \mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^2 \)) while moving a volumetric flow rate of \( Q = 5.0 \ \mathrm{m}^3/\mathrm{s} \). If the fan efficiency is \( \eta_f = 0.75 \), what is the required fan power (\( \dot{W} \))?

Air enters an ideal isothermal compressor (\( \eta_c = 1.0 \)) at a temperature of \( T_i = 293 \ \mathrm{K} \) and a mass flow rate of \( \dot{m} = 0.24 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{s} \). The pressure ratio from exit to inlet is \( P_e / P_i = 6.0 \). The universal gas constant is \( \bar{R} = 8314 \ \mathrm{J}/(\mathrm{kmol}\cdot\mathrm{K}) \) and the molecular weight of air is \( M = 29 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{kmol} \). Calculate the power consumed (\( |\dot{W}_{comp}| \)).

A primary air compressor in a manufacturing plant’s pneumatic system draws in ambient air (\( k = 1.4 \)) at an absolute inlet pressure of \( P_i = 100 \ \mathrm{kPa} \). Sensors indicate that the mass flow rate entering the unit is \( \dot{m} = 0.24 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{s} \) with a corresponding inlet density of \( \rho_i = 1.2 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^3 \). The air is then compressed and discharged into a receiver tank at a pressure of \( P_e = 600 \ \mathrm{kPa} \). Assuming the compression process is adiabatic and the machine operates at an ideal isentropic efficiency of \( \eta_c = 1.0 \), what is most nearly the mechanical power (\( |\dot{W}_{comp}| \)) required to drive this compressor?

An industrial cooling system is currently equipped with an oversized centrifugal pump featuring a \( D_1 = 10.0 \ \mathrm{in.} \) diameter impeller. Under baseline continuous operation, the pump draws a brake power of \( \dot{W}_1 = 15 \ \mathrm{hp} \). To optimize system efficiency and eliminate excessive throttling valve losses, plant engineers decide to physically trim the pump’s impeller down to a new diameter of \( D_2 = 9.0 \ \mathrm{in.} \). Assuming the pump continues to be driven at the exact same rotational speed (\( N_2 = N_1 \)) and handles the same fluid (\( \rho_2 = \rho_1 \)), what is most nearly the expected new power requirement (\( \dot{W}_2 \)) ?

A municipal water treatment plant needs to increase its daily throughput. An existing centrifugal pump currently operates at a rotational speed of \( N_1 = 1750 \ \mathrm{rpm} \) and delivers a baseline flow rate of \( Q_1 = 400 \ \mathrm{GPM} \). To meet the new capacity demands, engineers install a Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) to increase the pump’s motor speed to \( N_2 = 2100 \ \mathrm{rpm} \). Assuming the impeller diameter (\( D \)) remains unchanged and the system curve is compatible, what is most nearly the new volumetric flow rate (\( Q_2 \)) delivered by the pump?

A pump system transports liquid fertilizer (\( \rho = 1150 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^3 \)). The system requires a flow rate of \( Q = 0.2 \ \mathrm{m}^3/\mathrm{s} \) and a total head increase of \( H = 30 \ \mathrm{m} \). The pump has an efficiency of \( \eta_{pump} = 0.78 \), and the electric motor has an efficiency of \( \eta_{motor} = 0.92 \). Following the sequential power definitions in the NCEES Handbook, what is most nearly the required purchased electrical power (\( \dot{W}_{purchased} \))?

A centrifugal pump operates continuously to extract water (\( \rho = 1000 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^3 \)). It delivers a steady volumetric flow rate of \( Q = 0.05 \ \mathrm{m}^3/\mathrm{s} \) against a total head increase of \( H = 45 \ \mathrm{m} \). What is most nearly the ideal fluid power (\( \dot{W}_{fluid} \)) imparted to the water?

An open basin supplies water to a pump. The atmospheric pressure is \( P_{atm} = 14.7 \ \mathrm{psia} \) and the fluid’s specific weight is \( \gamma = 62.4 \ \mathrm{lbf}/\mathrm{ft}^3 \). The fluid vapor pressure is \( P_{vapor} = 0.26 \ \mathrm{psia} \). The pump is installed with a suction lift, meaning the water surface is \( 8.0 \ \mathrm{ft} \) below the pump impeller centerline. Total friction losses in the suction line are \( \Sigma h_L = 2.5 \ \mathrm{ft} \). What is most nearly the Net Positive Suction Head Available (\( NPSH_A \))?

A civil engineering irrigation project requires flow regulation between a primary upstream reservoir and a secondary downstream basin. The system utilizes a submerged circular orifice connecting the two bodies of water. The steady water level in the upstream reservoir is \( h_1 = 4.5 \ \mathrm{m} \) above the orifice centerline, while the downstream level is \( h_2 = 1.5 \ \mathrm{m} \) above the centerline. If the physical area of the orifice is \( A_0 = 0.5 \ \mathrm{m}^2 \) and the calibrated coefficient of discharge is \( C = 0.65 \), what is most nearly the steady volumetric flow rate (\( Q \)) passing through the submerged orifice?

A large primary clarifier tank in a wastewater treatment facility is equipped with a circular side drain. The fluid discharges freely into the atmosphere as a jet. The vertical distance from the constant water surface level to the centerline of the orifice is \( h = 5.0 \ \mathrm{m} \). The physical area of the orifice is \( A_0 = 0.02 \ \mathrm{m}^2 \), and the overall orifice coefficient (coefficient of discharge) is known to be \( C = 0.60 \). Assuming steady conditions, what is most nearly the volumetric flow rate (\( Q \)) exiting the tank?

A sharp-edged circular orifice is installed on the side of a large holding tank to discharge fluid. Because the upstream area (\( A_1 \)) of the tank is significantly larger than the orifice area (\( A_0 \)), the velocity of approach factor is considered negligible (\( A_0/A_1 \approx 0 \)). Engineers observe that the fluid streamlines continue to converge after passing through the opening, forming a “vena contracta”. The physical diameter of the orifice hole is \( D_0 = 100 \ \mathrm{mm} \). Experimental calibration shows that the coefficient of velocity is \( C_v = 0.98 \) and the overall coefficient of discharge is \( C = 0.61 \). What is most nearly the cross-sectional area of the fluid jet at the vena contracta (\( A_2 \))?

A municipal water treatment plant uses a primary horizontal Venturi meter to measure main line flow. The main pipe has an internal diameter of \( D_1 = 0.30 \ \mathrm{m} \), and it smoothly tapers to a throat diameter of \( D_2 = 0.15 \ \mathrm{m} \). Differential pressure taps indicate a pressure drop between the inlet and the throat of \( \Delta P = P_1 – P_2 = 25 \ \mathrm{kPa} \). The water density is \( \rho = 1000 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^3 \). If the calibrated coefficient of velocity for this specific meter is \( C_v = 0.98 \), what is most nearly the steady volumetric flow rate (\( Q \))?

A simple Pitot tube is placed in an open water channel to measure the steady flow velocity. The water (\( \rho = 1000 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^3 \)) has a static pressure at the measurement depth of \( P_s = 104.0 \ \mathrm{kPa} \). The stagnation pressure measured at the tip of the tube is \( P_0 = 108.5 \ \mathrm{kPa} \). What is most nearly the velocity (\( v \)) of the water stream?

A concrete dam has a fully submerged discharge orifice with a cross-sectional area of \( 0.15 \, \mathrm{m^2} \). The water depth on the upstream side of the orifice is \( 6.0 \, \mathrm{m} \), and the water depth on the downstream side is \( 1.5 \, \mathrm{m} \), both measured from the centerline of the orifice. If the discharge coefficient for this orifice is \( 0.80 \), the expected volumetric flow rate is most nearly:

A hydraulic engineer is testing a scale model of an open water channel. The prototype channel is scaled down to a model with a characteristic length ratio (\( L_p : L_m \)) of \( 12:1 \). The design velocity of the actual water flow in the full-scale prototype is \( 8 \, \mathrm{m/s} \). Assuming both the prototype and the model use water at the same temperature, determine the required flow velocity in the model to achieve dynamic similarity based on equal Reynolds numbers. The model velocity is most nearly:

An engineer is conducting a hydraulic model study for a proposed concrete gravity dam. The physical model is built to a geometric scale of 1:14. To maintain dynamic similarity for open channel flow over the spillway, Froude number scaling is applied. During testing, the water velocity at the toe of the model spillway is measured at \( 4.8 \, \mathrm{m/s} \). What is the anticipated velocity at the corresponding location on the full-scale prototype dam?

An aerospace engineering team is designing a high-altitude, long-endurance (HALE) unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). The wing has a tip-to-tip span length of \( b = 24.0 \ \mathrm{m} \) and a projected plan area of \( A_p = 36.0 \ \mathrm{m}^2 \). What is the aspect ratio (\( AR \)) of this wing?

During a wind tunnel test, a scaled prototype wing is subjected to an airflow with a density of \( \rho = 1.20 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^3 \) at a velocity of \( v = 80 \ \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s} \). The wing has a projected plan area of \( A_p = 2.5 \ \mathrm{m}^2 \). The load cells in the tunnel measure a total drag coefficient of \( C_D = 0.035 \) for this specific configuration. What is most nearly the total drag force (\( F_D \)) acting on the wing?

A light utility aircraft is cruising at a steady altitude where the ambient air density is \( \rho = 1.15 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^3 \). The aircraft has a true airspeed of \( v = 60 \ \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s} \) and a projected wing plan area of \( A_p = 16.0 \ \mathrm{m}^2 \). At this specific angle of attack, the aerodynamic lift coefficient for the wing is \( C_L = 0.55 \). What is most nearly the total lift force (\( F_L \)) generated by the wing?

id: 0599. Approximate Solution for Solid with Sudden Convection
stem: A solid sphere (\(r_o = 50\ \text{mm}\)) is initially at \(T_i = 250^\circ\text{C}\). It is exposed to convection such that \(Bi = 1.0\). At a dimensionless time of \(Fo = 0.5\), what is the center temperature (\(T_o\)) of the sphere? Assume \(T_{\infty} = 25^\circ\text{C}\).
sourceTags: Approximate Solution for Solid with Sudden Convection

id: 0598. Approximate Solution for Solid with Sudden Convection
stem: A long cylinder is cooling in a medium such that the Biot number is calculated to be \(Bi = 1.0\). Determine \(\zeta_1\) and \(C_1\).
sourceTags: Approximate Solution for Solid with Sudden Convection

id: 0597. Approximate Solution for Solid with Sudden Convection
stem: A large plane wall of thickness \(2L = 0.2\ \text{m}\) (\(L = 0.1\ \text{m}\)) has a thermal diffusivity of \(\alpha = 1 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}\). What is the Fourier number (\(Fo\)) at time \(t = 5\ \text{minutes}\)?
sourceTags: Approximate Solution for Solid with Sudden Convection

id: 0596. Transient Conduction Using the Lumped Capacitance Model
stem: A 2 kg steel block (\(c = 500\ \text{J}/(\text{kg}\cdot\text{K})\)) is initially at \(400^\circ\text{C}\). It is quenched in an oil bath at \(50^\circ\text{C}\). Assuming the lumped capacitance model is valid, what is the total amount of heat energy (\(Q_{total}\)) transferred from the block to the oil when the block reaches thermal equilibrium?
sourceTags: Transient Conduction Using the Lumped Capacitance Model

stem: A copper pin fin (\(k = 400\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)) has a diameter of \(2\ \text{mm}\) and a length of \(20\ \text{mm}\). The base temperature is \(100^\circ\text{C}\) and the ambient air is \(20^\circ\text{C}\) with \(h = 25\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Using the adiabatic tip assumption with corrected length, calculate the heat loss from the fin.

A cylindrical pin fin made of aluminum (\(k = 200\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)) has a diameter of \(D = 5\ \text{mm}\). The convection heat transfer coefficient is \(h = 40\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Calculate the fin parameter \(m\).

A steam pipe is covered with insulation. The pipe can be modeled as a cylindrical wall with an inner radius \(r_1 = 0.05\ \text{m}\), an outer radius \(r_2 = 0.10\ \text{m}\), and a length \(L = 5\ \text{m}\). The thermal conductivity of the insulation is \(k = 0.5\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\). The inner surface temperature is \(150^\circ\text{C}\) and the outer surface temperature is \(50^\circ\text{C}\). Calculate the rate of heat loss from the pipe.

Two aluminum plates (\(k = 240\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)), each \(2\ \text{cm}\) thick, are bolted together. The contact pressure results in a thermal contact conductance of \(h_c = 10,000\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\) at the interface. The outer surface of the first plate is at \(400^\circ\text{C}\), and the outer surface of the second plate is at \(300^\circ\text{C}\). Calculate the rate of heat transfer per unit area (heat flux) through the plates.

A “pin fin” (cylindrical cross-section) has a diameter \(D = 10\ \text{mm}\) and a length \(L = 40\ \text{mm}\). When performing heat transfer calculations using the corrected length method described in the NCEES Handbook, what is the value of \(L_c\)?

A rectangular aluminum fin (\(k = 200\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)) has a thickness of \(2\ \text{mm}\), a length of \(50\ \text{mm}\), and a width of \(1\ \text{m}\). The base temperature is \(150^\circ\text{C}\) and the fluid temperature is \(50^\circ\text{C}\) with \(h = 50\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Assuming  negligible heat transfer from tip, calculate the heat transfer rate from the fin.

id: 0577. Approximate Solution for Solid with Sudden Convection
stem: A large plane wall of thickness \(2L = 0.1\ \text{m}\) is initially at a uniform temperature of \(T_i = 300^\circ\text{C}\). It is suddenly exposed to convection on both sides with \(T_\infty = 30^\circ\text{C}\) and \(h = 400\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). The properties of the wall are \(k = 20\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\) and \(\alpha = 1 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}\). Calculate the temperature at the midplane (\(T_0\)) after \(125\ \text{s}\).
sourceTags: Approximate Solution for Solid with Sudden Convection

id: 0576. Transient Conduction Using the Lumped Capacitance Model
stem: Which of the following conditions must be satisfied for the lumped capacitance method to be considered valid for transient heat transfer analysis?
sourceTags: Transient Conduction Using the Lumped Capacitance Model

stem: A small copper ball (\(\rho = 8900\ \text{kg/m}^3\), \(c_p = 380\ \text{J}/(\text{kg}\cdot\text{K})\)) with a diameter of \(10\ \text{mm}\) is initially at \(250^\circ\text{C}\). It is dropped into an oil bath at \(30^\circ\text{C}\) with \(h = 40\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Assuming the lumped capacitance model is valid, calculate the time constant (\(\tau\)) for this cooling process.
sourceTags: Transient Conduction Using the Lumped Capacitance Model

id: 0574. Transient Conduction Using the Lumped Capacitance Model
stem: A solid steel sphere with a diameter of \(12\ \text{mm}\) is cooling in air. The thermal conductivity of steel is \(k = 40\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\) and the convection coefficient is \(h = 20\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Calculate the Biot number (\(Bi\)) for this process.
sourceTags: Transient Conduction Using the Lumped Capacitance Model

stem: A steam pipe with an outer diameter of \(60\ \text{mm}\) is covered with insulation having a thermal conductivity \(k = 0.15\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\). The convection heat transfer coefficient to the surrounding air is \(h = 10\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). If the thickness of the insulation is increased from \(5\ \text{mm}\) to \(10\ \text{mm}\), how is the heat transfer rate affected?

A plane wall with a thickness of \(L = 0.1\ \text{m}\) and thermal conductivity \(k = 1.0\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\) separates two fluids. Fluid 1 is at \(T_{\infty,1} = 200^\circ\text{C}\) with \(h_1 = 50\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Fluid 2 is at \(T_{\infty,2} = 50^\circ\text{C}\) with \(h_2 = 20\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Calculate the total thermal resistance per unit area (\(R_{total}\)) for this system.

A composite wall is composed of three layers. Layer 1 has \(R_1 = 0.5\ \text{K/W}\), Layer 2 has \(R_2 = 1.0\ \text{K/W}\), and Layer 3 has \(R_3 = 0.5\ \text{K/W}\). If the temperature of the outer surface of Layer 1 is \(400^\circ\text{C}\) and the outer surface of Layer 3 is \(100^\circ\text{C}\), what is the temperature drop across Layer 2?

An insulating material is needed to limit heat loss through a wall to \(200\ \text{W/m}^2\). The temperature difference across the insulation is \(50^\circ\text{C}\). If the thermal conductivity of the material is \(k = 0.04\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\), what is the minimum required thickness?

Heat is flowing through a large plate with a thickness of \(L = 50\ \text{mm}\). The thermal conductivity is \(k = 15\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\). The rate of heat transfer per unit area is measured to be \(\frac{\dot{Q} }{A} = 6000\ \text{W/m}^2\). If the hotter surface is at \(120^\circ\text{C}\), what is the temperature of the colder surface?

A plane wall (\(k = 0.8\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)) is \(20\ \text{cm}\) thick. The inner surface is kept at \(150^\circ\text{C}\). The outer surface is exposed to air at \(20^\circ\text{C}\) with a convection coefficient of \(h = 10\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Calculate the temperature of the outer surface (\(T_s\)).

A steel pipe (\(k = 50\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)) has an inner radius of \(2\ \text{cm}\) and an outer radius of \(2.5\ \text{cm}\). It is covered with a layer of insulation (\(k = 0.1\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)) that is \(1\ \text{cm}\) thick. The pipe is \(10\ \text{m}\) long. If the inner surface temperature of the pipe is \(200^\circ\text{C}\) and the outer surface temperature of the insulation is \(30^\circ\text{C}\), what is the total heat loss rate?

A hot water pipe (\(r_{outer} = 2\ \text{cm}\)) is covered with insulation (\(k = 0.1\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)) having an outer radius of \(4\ \text{cm}\). The length is \(10\ \text{m}\). The convection heat transfer coefficient on the outer surface is \(h = 10\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Calculate the total thermal resistance (\(R_{total}\)) of the insulation and convection.

A copper wire has a radius of \(r_{wire} = 3\ \text{mm}\). It is covered with insulation that has a critical radius of \(r_{cr} = 10\ \text{mm}\). If the thickness of the insulation is increased such that the outer radius goes from \(5\ \text{mm}\) to \(7\ \text{mm}\), what happens to the heat transfer rate?

choices.B: The heat transfer rate remains constant.

stem: An electric wire is being covered with plastic insulation having a thermal conductivity of \(k_{ins} = 0.15\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\). Post-loading measurements show the diameter has decreased to \( 0.02198\,\mathrm{m} \) and the length has increased to \( 2.11\,\mathrm{m} \). The engineering axial strain on the rod is most nearly:

A tensile force of \( 130 \, \mathrm{kN} \) is applied to a rod with an initial diameter of \( 0.025 \, \mathrm{m} \) and an initial length of \( 2.5 \, \mathrm{m} \). After applying the load, the diameter decreases to \( 0.02498 \, \mathrm{m} \), and the length increases to \( 2.52 \, \mathrm{m} \). The engineering stress on the rod is most nearly:

A structural tie rod with an initial diameter of \( 0.03\,\mathrm{m} \) and an original length of \( 3\,\mathrm{m} \) is subjected to a static tensile force of \( 150\,\mathrm{kN} \). Post-loading measurements show the diameter has decreased to \( 0.02998\,\mathrm{m} \) and the length has increased to \( 3.01\,\mathrm{m} \). The engineering stress experienced by the rod is most nearly:

A cylindrical steel tie rod undergoes a destructive tensile test in a laboratory. The initial diameter of the test specimen is measured as \( 0.500\,\mathrm{in} \). At the point of fracture, the necked-down region has a final diameter of \( 0.400\,\mathrm{in} \). The percent reduction in area (\( \%RA \)) for this specimen is most nearly:

A steel cable is used to lift a load of \( 25 \, \mathrm{kN} \). The cable has an initial length of \( 15 \, \mathrm{m} \) and a modulus of elasticity of \( 200 \, \mathrm{GPa} \). If the maximum allowable elastic longitudinal deformation is \( 10 \, \mathrm{mm} \), what is the minimum required diameter of the cable?

A \( 0.6 \, \mathrm{m} \) long solid steel rod has a diameter of \( 0.04 \, \mathrm{m} \) and a modulus of elasticity of \( 200 \, \mathrm{GPa} \). The rod supports an axial compressive load of \( 15,000 \, \mathrm{N} \). What is most nearly the decrease in the steel rod’s length?
A material experiences a shear stress of \( \tau_{xy} = 40 \, \mathrm{MPa} \) and has a shear modulus of \( G = 80 \, \mathrm{GPa} \). The shear strain is most nearly:

A metal rod, 5 meters in length, is firmly supported by two rigid supports at both ends. The rod has a coefficient of thermal expansion of \(11.7 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{per}^\circ \text{C}\), and its elastic modulus is \(210 \, \text{GPa}\). When the temperature of the rod increases by \(50^\circ \text{C}\), determine the thermal stress that develops in the rod due to the expansion being restricted by the supports.

A 5-m metal rod has a coefficient of thermal expansion and contraction of

\(11.7 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{per}^\circ \text{C}\). If the temperature of the rod is decreased

by \(50^\circ \text{C}\), the thermal strain is most nearly:

A pressure (150 psi) applied to a cylindrical vessel (the inner diameter:3 ft, the wall thickness:1 inch), a crack was developed longitudinally at the vessel wall. The failure/cracking stress in psi of the thin-walled pressure vessel is:

A mechanical engineer is evaluating a compressed air storage cylinder in a manufacturing facility. The cylindrical tank has an internal diameter of \( 720 \, \mathrm{mm} \) and is fabricated from \( 15\text{-}\mathrm{mm} \) thick structural steel plate. If the pressure gauge on the manifold reads an internal pressure of \( 1,700 \, \mathrm{kPa} \), the maximum tangential (hoop) stress developed in the cylindrical wall is most nearly:

A planar stress element on the web of a bridge girder has the following stresses applied due to combined bending and shear: \( \sigma_x = 90 \ \mathrm{MPa} \), \( \sigma_y = 30 \ \mathrm{MPa} \), and \( \tau_{xy} = 40 \ \mathrm{MPa} \). To determine the optimal orientation for placing carbon fiber reinforcement, find the angle \( \theta_{p1} \) to the principal plane experiencing the maximum principal stress. (Provide the smallest positive angle).

A thick-walled steel cylinder is subjected to internal pressure and an applied external torque. At a critical location on the outer surface, the combined loading produces a state of plane stress with components \( \sigma_x = 150 \ \mathrm{MPa} \), \( \sigma_y = 50 \ \mathrm{MPa} \), and \( \tau_{xy} = 40 \ \mathrm{MPa} \). To evaluate the cylinder’s safety using the Maximum Shear Stress (Tresca) yield criterion, calculate the maximum in-plane shear stress \( \tau_{\mathrm{max}} \).

A strain gauge rosette is attached to the surface of a loaded aircraft wing spar. The measured and transformed plane stress components at this critical location are found to be \( \sigma_x = -8 \ \mathrm{ksi} \), \( \sigma_y = 12 \ \mathrm{ksi} \), and \( \tau_{xy} = 10 \ \mathrm{ksi} \). To evaluate the material against a specific compressive failure theory, determine the minimum (most compressive) principal stress.

An element is subjected to a normal tensile stress \( \sigma_x = 120 \ \mathrm{ksi} \), a normal compressive stress \( \sigma_y = -60 \ \mathrm{ksi} \), and a shear stress \( \tau_{xy} = 40 \ \mathrm{ksi} \). What is the maximum principal stress (\( \sigma_1 \))?

A spherical pressure vessel experiences a state of equal biaxial tension. The stresses on a given element are \( \sigma_x = 60 \ \mathrm{MPa} \), \( \sigma_y = 60 \ \mathrm{MPa} \), and there is no shear stress (\( \tau_{xy} = 0 \)). Determine the principal stresses.

A thin-walled tube is subjected to pure torsion, resulting in a state of pure shear. The normal stresses are \( \sigma_x = 0 \) and \( \sigma_y = 0 \), and the shear stress is \( \tau_{xy} = 50 \ \mathrm{MPa} \). What are the principal normal stresses \( \sigma_1, \sigma_2 \) at this point?

An element of material is subjected to biaxial compression and shear. The stresses are \( \sigma_x = -50 \ \mathrm{MPa} \), \( \sigma_y = -30 \ \mathrm{MPa} \), and \( \tau_{xy} = 20 \ \mathrm{MPa} \). Find the principal stresses \( \sigma_1 \) and \( \sigma_2 \).

A point on a free surface is subjected to uniaxial tension \( \sigma_x = 100 \ \mathrm{MPa} \) and a negative shear stress \( \tau_{xy} = -40 \ \mathrm{MPa} \). There is no stress applied in the y-direction (\( \sigma_y = 0 \)). Calculate the maximum and minimum principal stresses at this point.

A structural component is subjected to a 2D plane stress state as shown. The normal stresses are \( \sigma_x = 80 \ \mathrm{MPa} \) and \( \sigma_y = 40 \ \mathrm{MPa} \), and the shear stress is \( \tau_{xy} = 30 \ \mathrm{MPa} \). Determine the maximum and minimum principal stresses (\( \sigma_1, \sigma_2 \)).
For a given state of plane stress at a point in a material, what is the magnitude of the in-plane shear stress on the principal planes where the principal normal stresses occur?

choices.A: It is equal to the maximum in-plane shear stress.
choices.B: It is equal to the average normal stress.
choices.D: It is equal to the maximum principal stress.

stem: A \( 3 \)-ft hollow circular shaft with an inner diameter of \( 14 \, \mathrm{in} \) and an outer diameter of \( 15 \, \mathrm{in} \) is subjected to a torsional moment of \( 12,000 \, \mathrm{kip \cdot ft} \). The shear modulus of the shaft material is \( 10,000 \, \mathrm{ksi} \). Determine the angle of twist of the shaft. The angle of twist is most nearly:
If a torque is applied to a circular shaft, the maximum shear stress is developed at:
answer:
FE Reference Handbook 10.3 P134,135:

Explanation: When a torque is applied to a circular shaft, the maximum shear stress occurs at the outer fiber of the shaft, farthest from the center. This is because shear stress due to torsion varies linearly with the radial distance from the center of the shaf

stem: Where can you find the maximum shear stress if a torque is applied to a circular shaft?

A hollow circular shaft has an inner diameter of \( 10 \, \mathrm{in} \) and an outer diameter of \( 11 \, \mathrm{in} \). A torsional moment of \( 150 \, \mathrm{kip \cdot ft} \) is applied to the shaft. Find the maximum shear stress developed in the shaft.

A hollow circular shaft has a length of \( 3\,\mathrm{ft} \), an inner diameter of \( 10\,\mathrm{in} \), and an outer diameter of \( 11\,\mathrm{in} \). The shaft is subjected to an applied torque of \( 10,000\,\mathrm{kip \cdot ft} \). If the shear modulus of the material is \( 10,000\,\mathrm{ksi} \), the angle of twist of the shaft is most nearly:

A solid aluminum rod has a shear modulus of \( G = 2.8 \times 10^{10} \, \mathrm{Pa} \), a diameter of \( 30 \, \mathrm{mm} \), and a length of \( 60 \, \mathrm{cm} \). One end is rigidly fixed to a support. Determine the approximate torque required at the free end to twist the rod by \( 5^\circ \) about its longitudinal axis. The required torque is most nearly:

A cantilever beam of length \( L = 6 \ \mathrm{m} \) is subjected to a uniform distributed load of \( w = 10 \ \mathrm{kN/m} \) over its entire length. In addition, a concentrated point load \( P = 25 \ \mathrm{kN} \) acts exactly at the midspan (\( a = 3 \ \mathrm{m} \) from the fixed support). The flexural rigidity is \( EI = 30,000 \ \mathrm{kN \cdot m^2} \). Determine the total maximum deflection \( v_{\mathrm{max}} \) at the free end.

A designer is selecting a cross-section for a cantilever beam of length \( L = 3 \ \mathrm{m} \). The beam must support a concentrated load \( P = 20 \ \mathrm{kN} \) at its free end. The material is steel with \( E = 200 \ \mathrm{GPa} \). To protect an adjacent glass panel, the maximum deflection at the free end is strictly limited to \( 5 \ \mathrm{mm} \). What is the minimum required moment of inertia \( I \) for the beam?

A cantilever beam of length \( L = 4 \ \mathrm{m} \) is subjected to a downward uniform distributed load of \( w = 8 \ \mathrm{kN/m} \). Simultaneously, an applied moment \( M_0 = 30 \ \mathrm{kN \cdot m} \) acts at the free end, creating an upward bending curvature (concave up). The flexural rigidity is \( EI = 10,000 \ \mathrm{kN \cdot m^2} \). Determine the magnitude and direction of the net deflection at the free end.

A “propped” cantilever beam of length \( L = 5 \ \mathrm{m} \) is fixed at the left end and subjected to a downward uniform distributed load of \( w = 24 \ \mathrm{kN/m} \). To prevent the free end from deflecting downward, an upward point load \( P \) is applied at the free end. What is the required magnitude of the upward force \( P \) so that the net deflection at the free end is exactly zero?

A cantilever beam of length \( L = 4 \ \mathrm{m} \) is loaded with both a uniform distributed load of \( w = 5 \ \mathrm{kN/m} \) over its entire length and a concentrated point load \( P = 10 \ \mathrm{kN} \) at its free end. The flexural rigidity is \( EI = 12,000 \ \mathrm{kN \cdot m^2} \). Using the principle of superposition, calculate the total maximum downward deflection \( v_{\mathrm{max}} \).

A cantilever beam of length \( L = 4 \ \mathrm{m} \) has an applied concentrated moment \( M_0 = 40 \ \mathrm{kN \cdot m} \) at its free end. The flexural rigidity of the beam is \( EI = 16,000 \ \mathrm{kN \cdot m^2} \). Calculate the maximum deflection \( v_{\mathrm{max}} \) at the free end.

A cantilever beam of length \( L = 5 \ \mathrm{m} \) is subjected to a concentrated load \( P = 50 \ \mathrm{kN} \) applied at a distance \( a = 3 \ \mathrm{m} \) from the fixed support. The flexural rigidity of the beam is \( EI = 25,000 \ \mathrm{kN \cdot m^2} \). Determine the maximum deflection \( v_{\mathrm{max}} \) at the free end of the beam.

A cantilever beam of length \( L = 3 \ \mathrm{m} \) is subjected to a uniform distributed load of \( w = 10 \ \mathrm{kN/m} \) over its entire length. The beam has a modulus of elasticity \( E = 200 \ \mathrm{GPa} \) and a moment of inertia \( I = 45 \times 10^6 \ \mathrm{mm^4} \). Calculate the maximum deflection \( v_{\mathrm{max}} \) at the free end.

A cantilevered steel beam of length \( L = 4 \ \mathrm{m} \) is subjected to a concentrated point load \( P = 15 \ \mathrm{kN} \) at its free end. The modulus of elasticity is \( E = 200 \ \mathrm{GPa} \) and the moment of inertia is \( I = 80 \times 10^6 \ \mathrm{mm^4} \). Determine the maximum downward deflection \( v_{\mathrm{max}} \) at the free end.

A machine component acts as a simply supported beam spanning \( L = 5 \ \mathrm{m} \). It is made of steel (\( E = 200 \ \mathrm{GPa} \)) and has a moment of inertia \( I = 100 \times 10^6 \ \mathrm{mm^4} \). To prevent interference with other moving parts, the maximum downward deflection at the center cannot exceed \( 10 \ \mathrm{mm} \). What is the maximum allowable magnitude of a point load \( P \) applied at the midspan?

A simply supported steel beam (\( E = 200 \ \mathrm{GPa} \)) spans \( L = 8 \ \mathrm{m} \) and is required to support a uniform distributed load of \( w = 12 \ \mathrm{kN/m} \). Building codes stipulate that the maximum allowable deflection is \( L/360 \). What is the minimum required moment of inertia \( I \) to satisfy this deflection criterion?

A simply supported beam of length \( L = 6 \ \mathrm{m} \) is subjected simultaneously to a uniform distributed load of \( w = 10 \ \mathrm{kN/m} \) and a concentrated point load of \( P = 30 \ \mathrm{kN} \) at the midspan. The flexural rigidity of the beam is \( EI = 24,000 \ \mathrm{kN \cdot m^2} \). Calculate the total magnitude of the end slope \( \theta \) at the supports.

A simply supported beam of length \( L = 6 \ \mathrm{m} \) is subjected simultaneously to a uniform distributed load of \( w = 10 \ \mathrm{kN/m} \) and a concentrated point load of \( P = 30 \ \mathrm{kN} \) at the midspan. The flexural rigidity is \( EI = 24,000 \ \mathrm{kN \cdot m^2} \). Calculate the total maximum deflection \( v_{\mathrm{max}} \) of the beam.

A simply supported beam of length \( L = 6 \ \mathrm{m} \) carries a uniform distributed load of \( w = 20 \ \mathrm{kN/m} \). The flexural rigidity of the beam is \( EI = 30,000 \ \mathrm{kN \cdot m^2} \). Calculate the magnitude of the slope \( \theta \) at either support.

A simply supported beam of length \( L = 5 \ \mathrm{m} \) is subjected to a concentrated point load \( P = 60 \ \mathrm{kN} \) at its midspan. The flexural rigidity of the beam is \( EI = 20,000 \ \mathrm{kN \cdot m^2} \). Determine the magnitude of the slope \( \theta \) at the supports.

A simply supported beam of length \( L = 8 \ \mathrm{m} \) carries a uniform distributed load of \( w = 15 \ \mathrm{kN/m} \) over its entire span. The beam’s modulus of elasticity is \( E = 200 \ \mathrm{GPa} \) and its moment of inertia is \( I = 250 \times 10^6 \ \mathrm{mm^4} \). Calculate the maximum deflection \( v_{\mathrm{max}} \).

A simply supported beam of length \( L = 6 \ \mathrm{m} \) is subjected to a concentrated point load \( P = 40 \ \mathrm{kN} \) at its midspan. The beam has a modulus of elasticity \( E = 200 \ \mathrm{GPa} \) and a moment of inertia \( I = 150 \times 10^6 \ \mathrm{mm^4} \). Calculate the maximum deflection \( v_{\mathrm{max}} \) of the beam.

A steel W-shape beam is reinforced by bolting two \( 10 \ \mathrm{in.} \times 1 \ \mathrm{in.} \) cover plates to its flanges. The total moment of inertia of the built-up section is \( I = 2,500 \ \mathrm{in^4} \). The distance from the neutral axis to the centroid of the top cover plate is \( 8.5 \ \mathrm{in.} \) If the section is subjected to a vertical shear of \( V = 120 \ \mathrm{kips} \), determine the total transverse shear flow \( q \) acting on the bolts connecting the top cover plate.

A built-up box beam is constructed by nailing two \( 100 \ \mathrm{mm} \times 20 \ \mathrm{mm} \) flange boards to two \( 10 \ \mathrm{mm} \times 140 \ \mathrm{mm} \) web boards as shown. The total moment of inertia is \( I = 36.0 \times 10^6 \ \mathrm{mm^4} \). The beam is subjected to a vertical shear force of \( V = 8.0 \ \mathrm{kN} \). If each nail can safely carry a shear force of \( F_{\mathrm{nail}} = 400 \ \mathrm{N} \), what is the maximum allowable longitudinal spacing \( s \) between the pairs of nails connecting the top flange to the webs?

A built-up wooden I-beam is constructed by gluing three boards together as shown. The beam is subjected to a vertical shear force of \( V = 25 \ \mathrm{kN} \). The total moment of inertia about the neutral axis is \( I = 55.6 \times 10^6 \ \mathrm{mm^4} \). Determine the shear flow \( q \) in the glue joint connecting the top flange to the web.

A hollow box beam has outer dimensions of \( B = 100 \ \mathrm{mm} \) (width) and \( H = 150 \ \mathrm{mm} \) (depth), with a uniform wall thickness of \( t = 10 \ \mathrm{mm} \). The calculated moment of inertia about the neutral axis is \( I = 13.48 \times 10^6 \ \mathrm{mm^4} \). If it carries a transverse shear force of \( V = 50 \ \mathrm{kN} \), calculate the maximum transverse shear stress.

A symmetric wide-flange beam (I-beam) is subjected to a transverse shear force of \( V = 150 \ \mathrm{kN} \). The moment of inertia about its neutral axis is \( I = 171.6 \times 10^6 \ \mathrm{mm^4} \). The cross-section dimensions are: flange width \( b_f = 200 \ \mathrm{mm} \), flange thickness \( t_f = 20 \ \mathrm{mm} \), overall depth \( d = 300 \ \mathrm{mm} \), and web thickness \( t_w = 10 \ \mathrm{mm} \). Calculate the transverse shear stress in the web, immediately below the junction with the top flange.

A symmetric wide-flange beam (I-beam) is subjected to a transverse shear force of \( V = 150 \ \mathrm{kN} \). The moment of inertia about its neutral axis is \( I = 171.6 \times 10^6 \ \mathrm{mm^4} \). The flange width is \( b_f = 200 \ \mathrm{mm} \), flange thickness is \( t_f = 20 \ \mathrm{mm} \), overall depth is \( d = 300 \ \mathrm{mm} \), and the web thickness is \( t_w = 10 \ \mathrm{mm} \). Calculate the maximum transverse shear stress in the beam (which occurs at the neutral axis).

A solid steel circular shaft is subjected to a transverse shear force of \( V = 20 \ \mathrm{kN} \). The diameter of the shaft is \( d = 40 \ \mathrm{mm} \). Determine the maximum transverse shear stress \( \tau_{\mathrm{max}} \) in the shaft.

A solid rectangular timber beam has a width of \( b = 50 \ \mathrm{mm} \) and a depth of \( h = 150 \ \mathrm{mm} \). If the beam is subjected to a maximum internal transverse shear force of \( V = 45 \ \mathrm{kN} \), determine the maximum transverse shear stress \( \tau_{\mathrm{max}} \) in the cross-section.

A structural beam is designed to carry a maximum internal bending moment of \( M_{\mathrm{max}} = 50 \ \mathrm{kN \cdot m} \). If the allowable normal bending stress for the material is \( \sigma_{\mathrm{allow}} = 150 \ \mathrm{MPa} \), what is the minimum required elastic section modulus \( S \) for the beam?

A hollow circular pipe functions as a structural beam and is subjected to a bending moment \( M = 30 \ \mathrm{kip \cdot in} \). The pipe has an outer diameter \( D = 4.0 \ \mathrm{in} \) and an inner diameter \( d = 3.0 \ \mathrm{in} \). Calculate the maximum bending stress on the cross-section.

An inverted T-beam is subjected to a positive internal bending moment of \( M = +25 \ \mathrm{kN \cdot m} \) (causing the beam to bend concave upward). The centroidal neutral axis (NA) is located \( 80 \ \mathrm{mm} \) from the top edge and \( 40 \ \mathrm{mm} \) from the bottom edge of the section. The moment of inertia about the NA is \( I = 8.0 \times 10^6 \ \mathrm{mm^4} \). Determine the magnitude of the maximum compressive bending stress in the cross-section.

A steel wide-flange beam (W-shape) is subjected to a maximum bending moment of \( M = 120 \ \mathrm{kip \cdot ft} \). The beam has an elastic section modulus \( S = 36.0 \ \mathrm{in^3} \) about its strong axis. Determine the maximum bending stress in the beam.

A simply supported timber beam with a solid rectangular cross-section is subjected to a maximum internal bending moment of \( M = 15 \ \mathrm{kN \cdot m} \). The cross-sectional dimensions are base \( b = 100 \ \mathrm{mm} \) and height \( h = 200 \ \mathrm{mm} \). Determine the maximum normal bending stress \( \sigma_{\mathrm{max}} \) in the beam.

The internal shear force in a simply supported beam is represented by the equation \( V(x) = 48 – 3x^2 \ \mathrm{kN} \), where \( x \) is measured in meters from the left support. Determine the location \( x \) where the maximum bending moment occurs within this region.

The shear force diagram for a beam region from \( x_1 = 0 \) to \( x_2 = 5 \ \mathrm{m} \) is defined by the equation \( V(x) = 30 – 6x \ \mathrm{kN} \). If the bending moment at the start of this region (\( x_1 = 0 \)) is \( M_1 = 15 \ \mathrm{kN \cdot m} \), determine the internal bending moment \( M_2 \) at \( x_2 = 5 \ \mathrm{m} \).

The internal bending moment in a structural member is expressed as \( M(x) = 4x^3 – 18x^2 + 15x – 30 \ \mathrm{kN \cdot m} \), where \( x \) is the position in meters. Determine the shear force \( V \) at \( x = 2 \ \mathrm{m} \).

The shear force in a continuous beam is defined by the equation \( V(x) = 120 – 10x – 2x^2 \ \mathrm{kN} \), where \( x \) is the distance in meters from the left support. Determine the magnitude of the distributed load \( w(x) \) acting on the beam at \( x = 3 \ \mathrm{m} \).

A rectangular beam has a width of \( b = 10 \,\text{in} \) and a total depth of \( h = 20 \,\text{in} \). At a certain section, the internal shear force is \( V = 18 \,\text{kips} \). Compute the maximum shear stress.

A steel W-shape column (\( E = 200 \ \mathrm{GPa} \)) has a total length of \( L = 8 \ \mathrm{m} \) and is pinned at both its top and bottom supports. The section properties are \( I_x = 150 \times 10^6 \ \mathrm{mm^4} \) (strong axis) and \( I_y = 30 \times 10^6 \ \mathrm{mm^4} \) (weak axis). To increase its capacity, a lateral brace is installed exactly at midspan (\( 4 \ \mathrm{m} \) from either end) that prevents displacement strictly in the weak-axis (y-y) direction. The brace does not prevent displacement in the strong-axis (x-x) direction. Calculate the critical buckling load \( P_{cr} \) for this braced column.

A steel structural member with a solid square cross-section (\( a = 50 \ \mathrm{mm} \)) acts as a pinned-pinned column. The modulus of elasticity is \( E = 200 \ \mathrm{GPa} \). If the column must be designed to withstand a critical buckling load of exactly \( P_{cr} = 150 \ \mathrm{kN} \), what is the maximum allowable length \( L \) of the column?

A solid circular column has a diameter of \( d = 80 \ \mathrm{mm} \) and a length of \( L = 2.5 \ \mathrm{m} \). The column is fixed at the base and completely free at the top. Calculate the maximum slenderness ratio (\( KL/r \)) for this column.

A rectangular timber column has cross-sectional dimensions of \( b = 60 \ \mathrm{mm} \) and \( h = 120 \ \mathrm{mm} \). It has an unbraced length of \( L = 3.5 \ \mathrm{m} \) and is pinned at both ends. The modulus of elasticity for the timber is \( E = 10 \ \mathrm{GPa} \). Determine the Euler critical buckling load \( P_{cr} \).

A steel column (\( E = 200 \ \mathrm{GPa} \)) with a length of \( L = 4.5 \ \mathrm{m} \) is pinned at both ends. The column must support a structural design load of \( P_{\mathrm{design}} = 400 \ \mathrm{kN} \). If safety standards mandate a Factor of Safety (FS) of 2.5 against Euler buckling, what is the minimum required moment of inertia \( I \) for the column’s cross-section?

An aluminum structural pipe (\( E = 70 \ \mathrm{GPa} \)) is used as a column with a length of \( L = 5 \ \mathrm{m} \). It is rigidly fixed at the base and pinned at the top. The pipe has an outside diameter \( D = 120 \ \mathrm{mm} \) and an inside diameter \( d = 100 \ \mathrm{mm} \). Calculate the critical buckling load \( P_{cr} \).

A steel W-shape column (\( E = 200 \ \mathrm{GPa} \)) has a length of \( L = 6 \ \mathrm{m} \) and is completely fixed at both ends. The cross-section properties are given as \( I_x = 80 \times 10^6 \ \mathrm{mm^4} \) (strong axis) and \( I_y = 15 \times 10^6 \ \mathrm{mm^4} \) (weak axis). Assume the column is completely unbraced along its entire length. Determine the critical buckling load \( P_{cr} \).

Two ideal, long columns have identical lengths, cross-sections, and are made of the same material. Column A is fixed at one end and pinned at the other. Column B is pinned at both ends. What is the theoretical ratio of the critical buckling load of Column A to Column B (\( P_{cr, A} / P_{cr, B} \))?

A timber post has a square cross-section with a side length of \( a = 150 \ \mathrm{mm} \). The post is fixed at the base and completely free at the top. The total length of the post is \( L = 3 \ \mathrm{m} \). Assuming the modulus of elasticity for the timber is \( E = 12 \ \mathrm{GPa} \), calculate the critical buckling stress \( \sigma_{cr} \).

A solid circular steel column has a diameter \( d = 100 \ \mathrm{mm} \) and a length \( L = 5 \ \mathrm{m} \). The column is pinned at both ends. Assuming the modulus of elasticity is \( E = 200 \ \mathrm{GPa} \), calculate the Euler critical buckling load \( P_{cr} \).

choices.D: Immediately Dangerous to Life and Health (IDLH)

stem: A worker comes into contact with a 60-Hz AC electrical circuit. According to the “Effects of Electrical Current on the Human Body” table, which current range corresponds to the “Let-go” threshold where a person can still voluntarily release the energized conductor?
Which of the following substances represents the highest toxicity (lowest lethal dose)?

A worker’s forearms (Surface Area \( SA = 2,000\ \mathrm{cm^2} \)) are in contact with wastewater containing a chemical at a concentration of \( 5.0\ \mathrm{mg/L} \). The chemical-specific permeability constant (\( PC \)) is \( 0.001\ \mathrm{cm/hr} \). The exposure occurs for 1 hour/day (\( ET \)), 250 days/year (\( EF \)) over 10 years (\( ED \)). The worker’s body weight (\( BW \)) is 70 kg, and the averaging time (\( AT \)) is 3,650 days (10 years). Using the handbook formula for Dermal contact with water, most nearly, what is the Absorbed Dose (AD)?

A chemical has a Cancer Slope Factor of \( 0.055\ (\mathrm{mg/kg\text{-}day})^{-1} \). If a resident’s calculated Chronic Daily Intake (CDI) is \( 0.004\ \mathrm{mg/kg\text{-}day} \), most nearly, what is the estimated incremental lifetime cancer risk?

A chronic toxicity study establishes a No-Observed-Adverse-Effect Level (NOAEL) of \( 50\ \mathrm{mg/kg\text{-}day} \) for a substance. To derive a human Reference Dose (RfD), uncertainty factors for interspecies variation (\( 10 \)) and intraspecies variation (\( 10 \)) are applied. Most nearly, what is the resulting RfD?

A child (15 kg) plays in soil contaminated with lead at a concentration of \( 400\ \mathrm{mg/kg} \). The child ingests \( 200\ \mathrm{mg} \) of soil per day for 350 days per year over a 6-year period. Assume the fraction ingested from the contaminated source (FI) is 1.0. Most nearly, what is the Chronic Daily Intake (CDI) for this child over the exposure duration?

Workers in a facility are exposed to toluene vapors. The average daily intake concentration is calculated to be \( 0.03\ \mathrm{mg/kg\text{-}day} \). The Reference Dose (RfD) for toluene is \( 0.08\ \mathrm{mg/kg\text{-}day} \). Most nearly, what is the Hazard Index (HI) for this exposure?

A groundwater supply is contaminated with arsenic at a concentration of \( 0.05\ \mathrm{mg/L} \). An adult resident (70 kg) consumes 2.0 L of this water daily for 20 years. The Cancer Slope Factor (CSF) for arsenic is \( 1.5\ (\mathrm{mg/kg\text{-}day})^{-1} \). Assume the averaging time for carcinogens is 70 years (25,550 days). Most nearly, what is the excess lifetime cancer risk for this resident?
A waste stream containing Cyanides (Group 11) is accidentally mixed with a waste stream containing Mineral Acids (Group 1). What are the potential consequences of this mixture?

choices.C: Generation of Toxic and Flammable Gas (GT, GF)

A system of forces acts on a structural plate. The system consists of two forces: \( 50 \ \mathrm{N} \) acting at coordinates \( (0, 5) \ \mathrm{m} \) in the positive x-direction, and \( -50 \ \mathrm{N} \) acting at coordinates \( (0, -5) \ \mathrm{m} \) in the negative x-direction. What is the magnitude of the couple?

A \( 50\,\mathrm{N} \) sphere is supported by two rigid, frictionless planes as shown in the figure. Plane \( AB \) is inclined at an angle of \( 30^\circ \) to the horizontal, while plane \( AC \) is perfectly vertical. Determine the most nearly correct horizontal and vertical reaction components at supports A and B for the given cable system.
