A square-thread screw-jack is used to lower a machine part. The load on the jack applied along and on the line of the axis is \( P = 10,000 \ \mathrm{N} \). The mean thread radius is \( r = 0.025 \ \mathrm{m} \) and the pitch angle of the thread is \( \alpha = 4^{\circ} \). If the appropriate coefficient of static friction is \( \mu = 0.15 \), what is the magnitude of the external moment \( M \) required for screw loosening?

An engineer applies an external moment of \( M = 40 \ \mathrm{N \cdot m} \) to the axis of a square-thread screw-jack to tighten it. The mean thread radius is \( r = 0.02 \ \mathrm{m} \), the pitch angle is \( \alpha = 5^{\circ} \), and the friction angle is \( \phi = 10^{\circ} \). What is the maximum load \( P \) on the jack applied along the line of the axis that can be lifted?

A square-thread screw-jack is used to raise a machine part. The load on the jack applied along and on the line of the axis is \( P = 10,000 \ \mathrm{N} \). The mean thread radius is \( r = 0.025 \ \mathrm{m} \) and the pitch angle of the thread is \( \alpha = 4^{\circ} \). If the appropriate coefficient of static friction is \( \mu = 0.15 \), what external moment \( M \) applied to the axis of the screw is required for screw tightening?

A belt runs over a stationary pulley with a contact angle of \( 120^{\circ} \). If the force applied to resist impending motion is \( F_2 = 150 \ \mathrm{N} \) and the coefficient of static friction is \( \mu = 0.25 \), what is the force \( F_1 \) required to initiate motion?

A worker is using a rope wrapped around a fixed cylindrical post to safely hold a heavy load. The load creates a force of \( F_1 = 3,000 \ \mathrm{N} \) in the direction of impending motion. The rope is wrapped around the post for exactly one full turn. If the coefficient of static friction between the rope and the post is \( \mu = 0.30 \), what is the minimum force \( F_2 \) the worker must apply to resist the impending motion?

A planar roof truss is subjected to a horizontal wind load \( P = 20 \ \mathrm{kN} \) at the top apex joint \( D \). It is supported by a pin at joint \( A \) and a roller at joint \( C \). Determine the internal axial force in the bottom chord member \( AB \).

A planar Pratt-style truss is subjected to a horizontal load of \( 15 \ \mathrm{kN} \) at joint \( D \) and a vertical point load of \( 40 \ \mathrm{kN} \) at joint \( B \). It is supported by a pin at \( A \) and a roller at \( C \). Determine the internal axial force in the diagonal member \( BF \).

A planar roof truss is subjected to a horizontal wind load \( P \) at the apex joint \( D \). It is supported by a pin at joint \( A \) and a roller at joint \( C \). Determine the internal axial force in the vertical member \( BD \).

A planar truss is loaded by a single vertical force \( P \) at joint \( E \). It is supported by a pin at \( A \) and a roller at \( C \). Determine the total number of zero-force members in this truss.

A unit moving load travels horizontally along the bottom chord (from joint \(A\) to joint \(E\)) of the planar Warren truss shown below. Determine the value of the influence line for the axial force in member \(CD\) when the unit load is located exactly at joint \(C\). Assume tension is positive and compression is negative.

A rigid vessel contains \(5\ \text{m}^3\) of a water–vapor mixture at a pressure of \(1.0021\ \text{MPa}\) with a quality of \(x_1 = 0.80\). The vessel is cooled at constant volume until the pressure drops to  \(0.4154\ \text{MPa}\). Determine the final mass (kg) of vapor and the final mass (kg) of liquid in the vessel.

A tank contains saturated liquid water at a pressure of \(0.4154\ \text{MPa}\). The total volume of the liquid is \(0.85\ \text{m}^3\). Heat is added at constant pressure until the water becomes completely vaporized. Determine the final volume \(V_2\) in \(\text{m}^3\) of the vapor.
A saturated water–vapor mixture is at \(140^\circ\text{C}\). The quality of the mixture is  \(x = 0.40\). Determine the specific volume \(v\) in   \(\text{m}^3/\text{kg}\).

A rigid tank contains a saturated water–vapor mixture at a temperature of  \(150^\circ\text{C}\). The quality of the mixture is \(x = 0.75\). Determine the specific volume \(v\) in \(\text{m}^3/\text{kg}\).

Nitrogen gas (Ideal Gas, \(R = 0.297\ \text{kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}\), \(c_p = 1.04\ \text{kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}\)) is compressed from \(100\ \text{kPa}, 300\ \text{K}\) to \(500\ \text{kPa}, 400\ \text{K}\). Determine the specific entropy change (\(\Delta s\)).

Calculate the Van der Waals constant \(a\) for Argon given its critical properties: \(P_c = 4.87\ \text{MPa}\), \(T_c = 150.8\ \text{K}\). Use the Universal Gas Constant \(\overline{R} = 8.314\ \text{kJ}/(\text{kmol}\cdot\text{K})\).

Determine the Van der Waals constant \(b\) for Nitrogen (\(N_2\)).The critical constants for nitrogen are \(P_c = 3.39\ \text{MPa}\) and \(T_c = 126.2\ \text{K}\). The Universal Gas Constant is \(\overline{R} = 8.314\ \text{kJ}/(\text{kmol}\cdot\text{K})\).

Nitrogen (\(N_2\)) is stored in a rigid container at a pressure of \(P = 10\ \text{MPa}\) and a temperature of \(T = 150\ \text{K}\). The critical constants for nitrogen are \(P_c = 3.39\ \text{MPa}\) and \(T_c = 126.2\ \text{K}\). The specific gas constant for nitrogen is \(R = 0.2968\ \text{kJ}/(\text{kg}\cdot\text{K})\). Using the Generalized Compressibility Chart, determine the specific volume \(v\) of the nitrogen at this state.

A laboratory chamber has interior dimensions of \(8\ \text{m} \times 5\ \text{m} \times 3\ \text{m}\). The chamber is maintained at a gage pressure of \(15\ \text{kPa}\), and the atmospheric pressure is \(100\ \text{kPa}\). The air temperature inside the chamber is \(32^\circ\text{C}\).

Assuming the molecular weight of air is \(M_{\text{air}} = 29\ \text{kg/kmol}\), determine the mass of air contained in the chamber.

A rigid air receiver (storage tank) has a volume of \(0.80\ \text{m}^3\). Initially, it contains air at an absolute pressure of \(100\ \text{kPa}\) and a temperature of  \(20^\circ\text{C}\).

A compressor then fills the tank with more air until the gage pressure in the tank is \(700\ \text{kPa}\). At the final state, the air temperature in the tank is \(60^\circ\text{C}\). 

Assuming air behaves as an ideal gas and has a molecular weight of  \(M_{\text{air}} = 28.97\ \text{kg/kmol}\), determine the mass of air added to the tank in kilograms.

A rigid pressure vessel has a fixed volume of \(3.5\ \text{m}^3\). The vessel contains nitrogen gas at an initial temperature of \(20^\circ\text{C}\) and a pressure of \(150\ \text{kPa}\). The gas is heated in the sealed vessel until the pressure reaches \(900\ \text{kPa}\). Assuming nitrogen behaves as an ideal gas and the mass in the vessel remains constant, determine the final temperature of the gas in degrees Celsius.

A high–pressure storage cylinder for compressed natural gas (CNG) has an inner diameter of \(0.30\ \text{m}\) and an internal length of \(1.2\ \text{m}\). The cylinder is initially evacuated and then filled with gas until the gage pressure reaches \(20\ \text{MPa}\) at a temperature of \(35^\circ\text{C}\).
Take the atmospheric pressure as \(100\ \text{kPa}\), and assume the gas is pure methane with molecular weight \(M = 16\ \text{kg/kmol}\). Assuming ideal-gas behavior, determine the mass of gas contained in the cylinder in kilograms.

A turbocharger compresses ambient air from an inlet pressure of \(p_1 = 95\ \text{kPa}\) to an outlet pressure of \(p_2 = 550\ \text{kPa}\) in a rapid, adiabatic, and isentropic process. The inlet air temperature is \(T_1 = 35^\circ\text{C}\). Assume that air behaves as an ideal gas with a specific heat ratio \(k = 1.4\). Determine the final air temperature in degrees Celsius.

A gas mixture is analyzed gravimetrically and found to contain 3 kg of nitrogen \((N_2)\), 5 kg of oxygen \((O_2)\), and 2 kg of carbon monoxide \((CO)\). Treating each component as an ideal gas, determine the gas constant  \(R_{\text{mix}}\) of the mixture in \(\text{kJ/(kg·K)}\).

Steam enters an adiabatic turbine at \(4\ \text{MPa}\) and \(400^\circ\text{C}\) (\(h_1 = 3214\ \text{kJ/kg}\)). The steam exits at a pressure where the isentropic enthalpy would be \(h_{2s} = 2100\ \text{kJ/kg}\). If the turbine has an isentropic efficiency of \(85\%\), determine the actual specific work output.

Two kilograms of Nitrogen gas expand in a piston-cylinder device at a constant pressure of \(500\ \text{kPa}\). The initial specific volume is \(0.1\ \text{m}^3/\text{kg}\) and the final specific volume is \(0.2\ \text{m}^3/\text{kg}\). During the process, \(150\ \text{kJ}\) of heat is added to the system. Determine the change in internal energy (\(\Delta U\)) of the nitrogen.

Steam enters a nozzle with an enthalpy of \(3,000\ \text{kJ/kg}\) and a velocity of \(50\ \text{m/s}\). It exits with a velocity of \(600\ \text{m/s}\). Neglecting heat transfer and potential energy, determine the specific enthalpy of the steam at the exit.

Air enters a compressor at \(298\ \text{K}\) and leaves at \(500\ \text{K}\). The mass flow rate of air is \(0.5\ \text{kg/s}\). Assume air behaves as an ideal gas with constant specific heats (\(C_p = 1.005\ \text{kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}\), \(C_v = 0.718\ \text{kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}\)). The compressor is adiabatic and kinetic/potential energy changes are negligible. Determine the power input required.

Refrigerant-134a is cooled by water in a condenser (heat exchanger). The refrigerant enters at \(10\ \text{kg/min}\) with an enthalpy change of \(\Delta h_R = -150\ \text{kJ/kg}\) (loss). Cooling water enters at \(20\ \text{kg/min}\). Assume the heat exchanger is insulated from the surroundings. What is the enthalpy change of the cooling water (\(\Delta h_w\))?
A) \(30\ \text{kJ/kg}\)

B) \(75\ \text{kJ/kg}\)

C) \(150\ \text{kJ/kg}\)

D) \(300\ \text{kJ/kg}\)

Steam enters a nozzle at \(400^\circ\text{C}\) and \(800\ \text{kPa}\) with a velocity of \(10\ \text{m/s}\). It leaves at \(300\ \text{kPa}\) and \(200^\circ\text{C}\). The inlet enthalpy is \(3267\ \text{kJ/kg}\) and the exit enthalpy is \(2865\ \text{kJ/kg}\). Neglecting heat transfer and potential energy changes, determine the exit velocity of the steam.
A) \(28.4\ \text{m/s}\)

B) \(804\ \text{m/s}\)

C) \(897\ \text{m/s}\)

D) \(804,000\ \text{m/s}\)

Refrigerant-134a flows through a throttling valve. Assuming the process is adiabatic and potential/kinetic energy changes are negligible, which property remains constant across the valve?
A) Pressure

B) Temperature

C) Enthalpy

D) Entropy

A closed piston-cylinder device contains a gas. During a process, \(50\ \text{kJ}\) of heat is added to the system, and the system does \(20\ \text{kJ}\) of work on the surroundings. What is the change in internal energy (\(\Delta U\)) of the system?
A) \(-30\ \text{kJ}\)

B) \(30\ \text{kJ}\)

C) \(70\ \text{kJ}\)

D) \(-70\ \text{kJ}\)

Steam enters an adiabatic turbine at a rate of \(10\ \text{kg/s}\). The inlet enthalpy is \(h_{i} = 3200\ \text{kJ/kg}\), and the exit enthalpy is \(h_{e} = 2100\ \text{kJ/kg}\). Neglecting changes in kinetic and potential energy, determine the power output of the turbine.
A) \(1,100\ \text{kW}\)

B) \(-11,000\ \text{kW}\)

C) \(11,000\ \text{kW}\)

D) \(53,000\ \text{kW}\)

One kilogram of saturated water–steam mixture is initially at \(70^\circ\text{C}\) with a quality of \(x = 0.25\). From the steam table, the saturation pressure at \(70^\circ\text{C}\) is \(31.19\ \text{kPa}\) and the specific volumes are  \(v_f = 0.001023\ \text{m}^3/\text{kg}\) and \(v_g = 5.042\ \text{m}^3/\text{kg}\). The mixture is heated at this constant pressure of \(31.19\ \text{kPa}\) until the temperature reaches \(200^\circ\text{C}\), at which point the steam is superheated. For the superheated state, assume ideal-gas behavior with \(R = 0.4615\ \text{kPa·m}^3/(\text{kg·K}) \). Using ideal-gas approximation for the final state, determine the work done (kJ) during the constant-pressure heating process.

A vertical cylinder with an inner diameter of \(0.12\ \text{m}\) initially contains  \(150\ \text{cm}^3\) of water at \(70^\circ\text{C}\). A \(40\ \text{kg}\) frictionless piston rests on top of the water and is exposed to the atmosphere. The system is slowly heated until the water temperature reaches \(220^\circ\text{C}\). Assume the following:
Determine the work in kJ done by the water during this process.

In an ideal Rankine cycle, steam leaves the boiler at \(h_3 = 3200\ \text{kJ/kg}\) and enters the condenser at \(h_4 = 2100\ \text{kJ/kg}\). The enthalpy of water leaving the condenser is \(h_1 = 200\ \text{kJ/kg}\), and the work input to the pump is \(5\ \text{kJ/kg}\) (so \(h_2 = 205\ \text{kJ/kg}\)). Determine the thermal efficiency of the cycle.
The ideal Otto cycle consists of four processes. Which of the following correctly describes the heat addition and heat rejection processes in this cycle?

choices.A: Constant Pressure Heat Addition, Constant Volume Heat Rejection
choices.B: Constant Volume Heat Addition, Constant Pressure Heat Rejection
choices.C: Constant Volume Heat Addition, Constant Volume Heat Rejection
choices.D: Constant Pressure Heat Addition, Constant Pressure Heat Rejection

stem: A heat pump is used to heat a house in winter and maintains a COP of \(3.5\). If the same cycle were used as an air conditioner (refrigerator) in summer operating between the same temperature limits, what would be its Coefficient of Performance?

A refrigerator operates on a reversed Carnot cycle between reservoirs at temperatures of \(25^\circ\text{C}\) and \(-10^\circ\text{C}\). What is the maximum theoretical Coefficient of Performance (\(\text{COP}_R\))?

A heat engine receives heat from a source at a rate of \(1000\ \text{kJ/min}\) and rejects waste heat to a sink at a rate of \(400\ \text{kJ/min}\). Determine the thermal efficiency and the power output of this engine.

A commercial refrigerator with a Coefficient of Performance (COP) of \(3.2\) is required to provide a cooling load of \(10\ \text{tons}\) of refrigeration. Determine the power input required to operate the compressor.

A heat engine operates on a Carnot cycle between a high-temperature source at \(600^\circ\text{C}\) and a low-temperature sink at \(40^\circ\text{C}\). What is the maximum theoretical thermal efficiency of this engine?

A Carnot heat pump is used to maintain a house at \(22^\circ\text{C}\) during the winter when the outside temperature is \(-5^\circ\text{C}\). Determine the maximum Coefficient of Performance ( \( COP_c \) ) of this heat pump.

At a total atmospheric pressure of \(90\ \text{kPa}\), moist air has a humidity ratio (\(\omega\)) of \(0.015\ \text{kg H}_2\text{O}/\text{kg dry air}\). Determine the partial pressure of the water vapor (\(P_v\)).

An HVAC system operates in a high-altitude location where the atmospheric pressure is \(80\ \text{kPa}\). Air is at \(25^\circ\text{C}\) with a relative humidity of \(50\%\). Given that the saturation pressure of water (\(P_g\)) at \(25^\circ\text{C}\) is \(3.169\ \text{kPa}\), calculate the humidity ratio (\(\omega\)).

Hot, dry air at \(95^\circ\text{F}\) dry bulb and \(70^\circ\text{F}\) wet bulb passes through an evaporative cooler (adiabatic saturation process) until the relative humidity reaches \(80\%\). What is the final dry-bulb temperature?

Air at \(50^\circ\text{F}\) dry-bulb and \(80\%\) relative humidity is heated sensibly to a final temperature of \(90^\circ\text{F}\) and \( 21\%\) relative humidity. Determine the heat added per pound of dry air (\(q = h_2 – h_1\)).
Air at \(50^\circ\text{F}\) dry-bulb and \(80\%\) relative humidity is heated sensibly to a final temperature of \(90^\circ\text{F}\). What is the new relative humidity?
Air at \(24^\circ\text{C}\) dry-bulb and \(60\%\) relative humidity is cooled at constant pressure. Determine the dew-point temperature (\(T_{dp}\)).
Measured air conditions are \(30^\circ\text{C}\) dry-bulb and \(20^\circ\text{C}\) wet-bulb. What is the approximate relative humidity?
Moist air exists at a dry-bulb temperature of \( 25^\circ\text{C}\) and a relative humidity of \(50\%\). Determine the specific enthalpy (\(h\)) of the air mixture.

id: 0535. Entropy Change for Solids and Liquids
stem: \(1\ \text{kg}\) of water at \(100^\circ\text{C}\) is mixed adiabatically with \(1\ \text{kg}\) of water at \(20^\circ\text{C}\) under constant pressure. Assume the specific heat of water is constant at \(c_p = 4.18\ \text{kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}\). Determine the total entropy generated during this mixing process.
On a Temperature-Entropy (T-s) diagram, an actual (adiabatic but irreversible) expansion process in a turbine is represented by a line that:

choices.B: Moves diagonally downwards to the right (Increasing s).
choices.C: Moves diagonally downwards to the left (Decreasing s).
choices.D: Moves horizontally to the right (Constant T).

stem: Heat is transferred from a reservoir at \(600\ \text{K}\) to a reservoir at \(300\ \text{K}\). The total entropy generation (\(\Delta S_{total}\)) for this process is calculated to be \(2.0\ \text{kJ/K}\). If the environmental dead state temperature is \(T_L = 298\ \text{K}\), determine the Irreversibility (\(I\)) of this process.

Steam enters a turbine with a specific enthalpy \(h = 3200\ \text{kJ/kg}\) and specific entropy \(s = 7.0\ \text{kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}\). The environmental “dead state” conditions are \(T_L = 298\ \text{K}\) (\(25^\circ\text{C}\)), \(P_L = 100\ \text{kPa}\), \(h_L = 105\ \text{kJ/kg}\), and \(s_L = 0.36\ \text{kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}\). Neglecting kinetic and potential energy, calculate the specific flow exergy (availability, \(\Psi\)) of the steam at the inlet.
Air (ideal gas, \(k=1.4\)) is compressed isentropically from \(100\ \text{kPa}\) and \(300\ \text{K}\) to \(500\ \text{kPa}\). Calculate the final temperature.

A \(5\ \text{kg}\) block of copper with a specific heat capacity of \(0.385\ \text{kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}\) is heated from \(27^\circ\text{C}\) to \(127^\circ\text{C}\). Determine the total change in entropy of the copper block.
An isolated system undergoes an irreversible process. Which of the following statements correctly describes the change in total entropy (\(\Delta S_{total}\))?

An inventor claims to have developed a heat engine that receives \(500\ \text{kJ}\) of heat from a geothermal source at \(150^\circ\text{C}\) and produces \(500\ \text{kJ}\) of work output per cycle, rejecting no waste heat to the surroundings. Which statement correctly evaluates this claim?

choices.A: The claim is valid because it satisfies the First Law of Thermodynamics (Energy Conservation).
choices.B: The claim is invalid because it violates the Kelvin-Planck statement of the Second Law.
choices.C: The claim is invalid because it violates the Clausius statement of the Second Law.
choices.D: The claim is valid if the engine operates reversibly.

stem: When calculating the standard heat of combustion for a hydrocarbon fuel using the Reference Handbook, the water in the products is typically assumed to be in which phase?

choices.D: A mixture of liquid and vapor

stem:
Determine the standard enthalpy of combustion (\(\Delta H_r^\circ\)) for the reaction: \(CO(g) + \frac{1}{2}O_2(g) \rightarrow CO_2(g)\).
Given Standard Enthalpies of Formation (\(\Delta H_f^\circ\)):

A combustion process utilizes \(25\ \text{kg}\) of air for every \(1\ \text{kg}\) of fuel. If the stoichiometric (theoretical) air-fuel ratio is calculated to be \(17.2\), determine the percent excess air.
Calculate the stoichiometric air-fuel ratio by mass for Methane (\(CH_4\)). Assume the molecular weight of air is \(29\ \text{kg/kmol}\) and Methane is \(16\ \text{kg/kmol}\).
Propane (\(C_3H_8\)) burns completely with the stoichiometric amount of air. Determining the coefficient of the nitrogen (\(N_2\)) term in the balanced product equation.

Estimate the saturation pressure \(P_2\) at \(T_2 = 350\ \text{K}\) given \(P_1 = 10\ \text{kPa}\) at \(T_1 = 300\ \text{K}\). Assume the heat of vaporization \(h_{fg}\) is constant at \(40\ \text{kJ/mol}\) and the gas constant \(R = 8.314\ \text{J/(mol}\cdot\text{K})\).

Using the Clapeyron equation, determine the slope of the saturation pressure-temperature curve \((dP/dT)_{sat}\) for a substance at a state where \(T = 300\ \text{K}\), \(h_{fg} = 2000\ \text{kJ/kg}\), and the change in specific volume upon vaporization \(v_{fg} = 2.5\ \text{m}^3/\text{kg}\).
Determine the number of degrees of freedom (\(F\)) for pure liquid water in equilibrium with its vapor (a saturated liquid-vapor mixture).

An air refrigeration cycle is used in heat pump mode to heat a cabin. The specific enthalpies are given as:
Determine the \(COP_{HP}\) for this cycle.

A two-stage heat pump operates with the following specific enthalpies:
Assume the mass flow rates are the same in each stage. Calculate the Coefficient of Performance for the heat pump (\(COP_{HP}\)).

An air refrigeration cycle operates between specific enthalpy limits. The enthalpy values are:
Determine the Coefficient of Performance (\(COP_{ref}\)) for this cycle.

Consider a two-stage refrigeration cycle with a flash chamber. Assume the mass flow rates are the same in each stage. The specific enthalpies at the key state points are given as:
Calculate the Coefficient of Performance for the refrigerator (\(COP_{ref}\)).

A civil engineering firm is submitting a proposal for a large municipal wastewater treatment plant. To make their proposal more attractive, the firm lists a renowned wastewater expert as a “Key Consultant” in their organizational chart. However, the firm has not actually contacted this expert or secured their agreement to work on the project. Is this action ethical according to the NCEES Model Rules?

choices.A: Yes, provided the firm fully intends to hire the expert if they win the contract.
choices.B: No, because it constitutes a misrepresentation of the firm’s professional qualifications and associations.
choices.C: Yes, because it is standard marketing practice to list potential team members in a proposal.
choices.D: No, unless the expert has previously worked with the firm on similar projects.

stem: Engineer A is competing with Engineer B for a lucrative contract. To improve his chances, Engineer A starts a rumor that Engineer B is currently under investigation for fraud, knowing this information is false. Is Engineer A’s conduct acceptable under the NCEES Model Rules?

choices.A: Yes, provided that Engineer A genuinely believes he is more qualified for the job than Engineer B.
choices.B: No, because licensees shall not maliciously or falsely attempt to injure the professional reputation of another licensee.
choices.C: Yes, because aggressive marketing strategies to highlight a competitor’s weaknesses are standard business practice.
choices.D: No, unless Engineer A submits a formal report to the state licensing board before spreading the rumor.

stem: A professional engineer is hired by a land developer to design a subdivision. The construction contractor, who is building the subdivision, also asks the engineer to perform a structural inspection on the same project and offers to pay him for this additional service. How should the engineer respond to the contractor’s offer?

choices.A: Accept the offer immediately, as inspections are separate from design work.
choices.B: Decline the offer unless the circumstances are fully disclosed and agreed to in writing by all interested parties.
choices.C: Accept the offer but request that the payment be made in cash to avoid a conflict of interest trail.
choices.D: Decline the offer strictly because accepting payment from two parties on the same project is never allowed.

stem: A Civil PE is the prime design professional for a commercial building project. The project includes structural, mechanical, and electrical components. The Civil PE signs and seals the civil and structural drawings, which he prepared. He also signs and seals the cover sheet for the entire set of plans, which includes the mechanical and electrical drawings prepared by other consultants. Is this action permissible?

choices.A: No, a licensee can never sign a document that contains work they did not personally prepare.
choices.B: Yes, provided that the mechanical and electrical drawings are each signed and sealed by their respective licensed professionals.
choices.C: Yes, because as the prime professional, he is automatically responsible for all technical aspects of the project.
choices.D: No, unless he possesses a license in all three disciplines (Civil, Mechanical, Electrical).

stem: John Doe graduated with a degree in civil engineering four years ago but has not yet passed the Principles and Practice of Engineering (PE) exam. He opens his own consulting business and prints business cards that read “John Doe, Civil Engineer.” In many jurisdictions based on the NCEES Model Law, is this permissible?

choices.A: Yes, because he has an accredited engineering degree.
choices.B: Yes, as long as he does not use the specific title “Professional Engineer” (PE).
choices.C: No, the use of the word “Engineer” in a business title offering services to the public is generally restricted to licensed individuals.
choices.D: No, unless he works under the direct supervision of a licensed PE in his own company.

stem: A civil engineer is overseeing the construction of a high-rise building. During excavation, the engineer discovers that the soil conditions are significantly worse than indicated in the geotechnical report. Strengthening the foundation will cost an additional $2 million and delay the project by two months. The developer insists on proceeding with the original design to avoid financial losses, claiming the risk is “acceptable.” What is the engineer’s ethical obligation?

choices.A: Proceed with the original design but document the developer’s decision in writing to limit liability.
choices.B: Refuse to approve the work and notify the local building department if the developer persists.
choices.C: Suggest a compromise design that saves some money but still does not fully meet the safety code.
choices.D: Resign from the project immediately without notifying anyone to avoid conflict.

stem: A civil engineering firm wants to win a contract for a new city park. The firm’s principal learns that the mayor, who has the final say on the contract award, is running for re-election. The principal donates a large sum of money to the mayor’s campaign with the specific intent of influencing the contract decision. This action is:

choices.A: Ethical, as long as the donation is within the legal limit for campaign contributions.
choices.B: Ethical, provided the firm is actually the most qualified for the job.
choices.C: Unethical, because it constitutes a political contribution made with the intent to influence the award of a contract.
choices.D: Unethical, but only if the mayor explicitly asked for the money.

stem: Engineer A is retained by a client to review a design prepared by Engineer B. During the review, Engineer A identifies a calculation error that significantly reduces the load-bearing capacity of the structure, posing a safety risk. According to the NCEES Model Rules, what is Engineer A’s obligation regarding Engineer B?

choices.A: Correct the error silently and seal the new plans without involving Engineer B.
choices.B: Make a reasonable effort to inform Engineer B of the error, unless legally prohibited.
choices.C: Report Engineer B immediately to the state board for incompetence before notifying the client.
choices.D: Inform the client but strictly avoid contacting Engineer B to prevent conflict.

stem: A licensed Professional Engineer is convicted of tax evasion, a felony charge unrelated to his engineering practice. The state licensing board initiates disciplinary action to revoke his license. The engineer argues that his license cannot be revoked because the crime did not involve engineering competence or safety. Is the board’s action justified?

choices.A: No, the board can only discipline licensees for negligence in engineering practice.
choices.B: No, personal financial crimes are outside the board’s jurisdiction.
choices.C: Yes, conviction of any felony is grounds for disciplinary action, regardless of its relation to engineering.
choices.D: Yes, but only if the tax evasion occurred while managing a client’s funds.

stem: A Professional Engineer is hired by a large chemical company to attend a town hall meeting and argue against a proposed environmental regulation that would increase the company’s costs. The engineer introduces himself as a “concerned expert citizen” but does not reveal that he is being paid by the chemical company to speak. According to the NCEES Model Rules, is this acceptable?

choices.A: Yes, because he is expressing his honest professional opinion based on facts.
choices.B: Yes, as long as he does not lie about the technical data.
choices.C: No, he must explicitly identify the interested party on whose behalf he is speaking.
choices.D: No, engineers are prohibited from speaking at political town hall meetings.

stem: Licensee A gains knowledge that Licensee B has falsified data in a geotechnical report submitted for a public school project. Licensee A knows this violation could compromise the building’s foundation. According to the NCEES Model Rules, what is Licensee A’s obligation?

choices.A: Confront Licensee B privately and ask him to fix the report.
choices.B: Ignore the situation to avoid damaging a professional colleague’s reputation.
choices.C: Report the violation to the licensure board and cooperate with their investigation.
choices.D: Anonymous leak the information to the school district’s principal.

stem: A Professional Engineer is asked by his supervisor to sign and seal a set of design drawings prepared by a junior engineer in a different branch office. The PE did not supervise the design process, did not review the calculations, and has not visited the site, but he trusts the junior engineer’s competence. Which of the following statements is true regarding the PE’s authority to seal these documents?

choices.A: He may seal them because the junior engineer works for the same company.
choices.B: He may seal them if he conducts a quick spot-check of the final drawings.
choices.C: He may not seal them because they were not prepared under his responsible charge.
choices.D: He may seal them provided the company assumes full liability insurance.

stem: Engineer X recently left Firm A to join Firm B. Firm B is now bidding on a project for a client that Engineer X worked with while at Firm A. Firm B asks Engineer X to share specific cost data and design details from the previous project to help them prepare a competitive bid. The data is not public record. How should Engineer X respond?

choices.A: Share the data since he was the original author of the design documents.
choices.B: Refuse to share the data unless he obtains prior consent from Firm A and the client.
choices.C: Share the data but remove the client’s name to maintain anonymity.
choices.D: Refuse to share the data unless the new project is identical to the old one.

stem: An engineer is part of a selection committee to award a construction contract for a new highway bridge. Upon reviewing the list of bidders, the engineer realizes that one of the construction firms is owned by his first cousin. The engineer believes he can remain impartial. According to the NCEES Model Rules, what must the engineer do?

choices.A: Recuse himself from the committee without explanation to maintain family privacy.
choices.B: Remain on the committee but vote against his cousin’s firm to prove impartiality.
choices.C: Disclose the relationship to his employer and the committee members immediately.
choices.D: Keep the relationship confidential since a cousin is not considered an immediate family member.

stem: A Professional Engineer (PE) licensed in Civil Engineering is asked by his firm to seal a set of electrical design drawings because the staff Electrical PE is currently hospitalized and the project deadline is today. The Civil PE has taken a few basic electrical courses in college but has no significant work experience in power systems. According to the NCEES Model Rules, what is the engineer’s most appropriate course of action?

choices.A: Seal the drawings to ensure the firm meets the deadline, provided the Electrical PE reviews them later.
choices.B: Refuse to seal the drawings because he lacks competence in the specific technical field.
choices.C: Seal the drawings but include a disclaimer stating that his expertise is primarily in Civil Engineering.
choices.D: Review the drawings for general compliance and then seal them under his responsible charge.

stem: Engineer B is responsible for selecting a vendor for a large municipal pump station project. One of the competing vendors, Vendor X, invites Engineer B to an all-expenses-paid “technical seminar” at a luxury golf resort in Hawaii. The seminar takes up two hours of the three-day trip. According to the NCEES Model Rules, Engineer B should:

choices.A: Accept the invitation provided the trip is disclosed to his employer.
choices.B: Accept the invitation but pay for his own airfare to show partial independence.
choices.C: Decline the invitation, as it constitutes a gratuity that could influence his judgment.
choices.D: Accept the invitation only if Vendor X is the lowest bidder.

stem: An engineer is hired as an expert witness by a plaintiff in a structural failure lawsuit. During the investigation, the engineer finds a report that suggests the plaintiff’s own lack of maintenance contributed significantly to the failure. This information hurts the client’s case. According to the NCEES Model Rules, the engineer must:

choices.A: Exclude this information from the testimony to protect the client’s interest.
choices.B: Include all relevant and pertinent information in an objective and truthful manner.
choices.C: Withdraw from the case to avoid a conflict of interest.
choices.D: Classify the report as a “trade secret” to prevent it from being entered into evidence.

stem: Engineer A works for a manufacturing company. She discovers that a chemical discharge valve is malfunctioning and releasing a level of toxins slightly above the EPA limit into a local river. She reports this to her plant manager, who tells her that fixing it would require a costly shutdown and that she should “let it go for now” since the excess is minimal. What is Engineer A’s obligation?

choices.A: Document the conversation with the manager in a personal log and take no further action.
choices.B: Immediately contact the local news media to expose the violation to the public.
choices.C: Notify the appropriate regulatory authority since the manager has refused to correct the safety hazard.
choices.D: Resign from the company to avoid legal liability.

stem: An engineer is retained by a developer to design a retaining wall for a residential community. During the design phase, the engineer discovers that the soil conditions on-site are unstable and require a more expensive reinforcement system than originally budgeted. The developer insists on using the cheaper, original design to stay within budget and assures the engineer that they will sign a liability waiver releasing the engineer from any future responsibility. How should the engineer respond?

choices.A: Proceed with the cheaper design after the waiver is signed and notarized to protect against lawsuits.
choices.B: Withdraw from the project immediately and maintain confidentiality regarding the soil conditions.
choices.C: Refuse to seal the plans and advise the developer that the design must be modified to ensure public safety.
choices.D: Seal the plans but attach a memo to the building department outlining the potential risks.

stem: An engineer is designing a chemical plant near a nature reserve. The design meets all federal emission standards. However, the engineer knows that even compliant emissions could harm a rare species of bird in the reserve over time. What should the engineer employ concern for:

choices.A: Compliance with the law only; exceeding standards is not required.
choices.B: Protection of ecosystems and environmental health.
choices.C: Maximizing shareholder value above all else.

stem: An engineer is evaluating two different materials for a new beverage container. Material A is cheaper to manufacture but difficult to recycle. Material B is more expensive to manufacture but is 100% recyclable and uses less energy during disposal. To make an ethical decision based on sustainable principles, the engineer should perform a:

choices.A: Cost-Benefit Analysis focused solely on production costs.

stem: A civil engineer is designing a roadway through a sensitive wetland area. The client requests a route that is the most cost-effective but would require draining a significant portion of the wetland, potentially destroying the local ecosystem. According to the principle of sustainable development in engineering, the engineer should:

choices.A: Follow the client’s instructions as long as the design meets minimum highway safety standards.
choices.B: Design the cheapest route but donate personal funds to a local environmental charity.
choices.C: Advise the client on the long-term environmental impact and propose an alternative route that minimizes ecosystem damage, even if it costs more.
choices.D: Refuse the project immediately because building near wetlands is always unethical.

stem: A company develops a new line of high-efficiency compressors and wants to protect the unique brand name and logo they have created for this product line to distinguish it from competitors. Which form of intellectual property protection is appropriate?
A company is granted a utility patent for a new hydraulic pump design in the United States. Assuming all maintenance fees are paid, how long does this patent protection generally last?

choices.A: 14 years from the date of issue.
choices.B: 17 years from the date of issue.
choices.C: 20 years from the date the application was filed.
choices.D: Indefinitely, as long as it is used in commerce.

stem: A mechanical engineer invents a new type of gear mechanism that significantly improves transmission efficiency. He also designs a unique, aesthetically pleasing casing for the gearbox that does not affect its function. To protect both the functional mechanism and the ornamental appearance, which types of patents should he apply for?

choices.A: Utility patent for the mechanism and Copyright for the casing.
choices.B: Utility patent for the mechanism and Design patent for the casing.
choices.C: Design patent for both the mechanism and the casing.
choices.D: Trade secret for the mechanism and Trademark for the casing.

stem: An engineer leaves Company A to work for a competitor, Company B. While at Company A, she developed a proprietary manufacturing process that gave Company A a significant economic advantage. This process was not patented but was kept confidential. Can she use this process at Company B?

choices.A: Yes, because it was not patented, it is public domain.
choices.B: Yes, because she developed it herself, she owns the intellectual property.
choices.C: No, because it is considered a Trade Secret of Company A.
choices.D: No, unless she changes at least 20% of the process steps.
